comp/closing-math.blurb: Debits, credits, prorations, and who pays what at the table.

examples.k: $2,880 as a SELLER DEBIT and BUYER CREDIT.
examples.s: Annual taxes $4,320, unpaid. Closing September 1; seller responsible through August 31; 360-day year.
w: Eight full months elapsed = 8 x $360 = $2,880
The bill is unpaid and the buyer will pay all of it later.

examples.k: $1,400 SELLER DEBIT / BUYER CREDIT - the reverse of a prepaid tax proration.
examples.s: $2,100 rent for a 30-day month, collected by the seller on the 1st. Closing on the 11th, buyer owns from closing day.
w: Buyer owns the 11th through the 30th = 20 days
20 x $70 = $1,400 belonging to the buyer
The seller is holding that cash.

examples.k: $23,850 to the table.
examples.s: $417,000 price, 95% LTV loan, $8,000 buyer closing costs, $5,000 earnest money already deposited.

ga: Georgia transfer tax on the statement: price / 1,000, as a SELLER debit.
Georgia taxes attach as a lien January 1 and are paid in arrears, so they normally produce a seller debit.
comp/closing-math.label: Closing & settlement math

check.q: The sale price appears as:
check.why: Everything else adjusts around this line.

check.q: The new loan is a:
check.why: The lender's money reduces what the buyer owes.

l: SALE PRICE - buyer DEBIT, seller CREDIT. The largest line, and everything else adjusts around it.
NEW LOAN - buyer CREDIT (the lender's money pays part of what the buyer owes).
EARNEST MONEY already on deposit - buyer CREDIT (already paid).
SELLER'S LOAN PAYOFF - seller DEBIT (comes out of the seller's proceeds).
COMMISSION - normally a seller DEBIT.
Georgia TRANSFER TAX - customarily a seller DEBIT, $1.00 per $1,000.
Recording the deed, loan charges, origination - normally buyer DEBITS.

check.q: Rent collected in advance by the seller produces a:
check.why: The seller is holding cash belonging to the buyer.

check.q: Prepaid insurance the buyer will benefit from produces a:
check.why: The seller is reimbursed - opposite to rent.

sections.h: The one question that settles every proration
l: UNPAID taxes (arrears) - the seller owes for their time but the buyer will pay the whole bill later: SELLER DEBIT / BUYER CREDIT.
PREPAID taxes or insurance - the seller paid for time the buyer will enjoy: SELLER CREDIT / BUYER DEBIT.

RENT collected in advance - the seller is holding the buyer's share: SELLER DEBIT / BUYER CREDIT. Rent runs OPPOSITE to prepaid taxes, because the money is cash in the seller's hand rather than a benefit already consumed.
SECURITY DEPOSITS - belong to the tenant; the buyer inherits the obligation: SELLER DEBIT / BUYER CREDIT. The tenant is not paid at closing.
ACCRUED INTEREST on an assumed loan - interest is paid in arrears, so the seller used the money but has not paid: SELLER DEBIT / BUYER CREDIT.
p: Ask: who currently HAS the money, and who will get the BENEFIT? Whoever holds money belonging to the other side is DEBITED.

check.q: Cash to close equals:
check.why: Credits include the loan and earnest money already paid.

sections.h: Cash to close and seller's net
l: Buyer's cash to close = (price + buyer costs) - (loan + earnest money + buyer credits)
Seller's net = price - payoff - commission - seller costs, adjusted for prorations

check.q: The banker's year used for prorations has:
check.why: Twelve 30-day months, unless told otherwise.

l: Daily rate = annual amount / 360 (banker's year) unless told otherwise.
Seller owns through the day BEFORE closing; buyer owns closing day forward.
Origination and points are a percentage of the LOAN, not the price.

comp/closing-math.summary: A settlement statement is two columns per party. A DEBIT is what you owe; a CREDIT reduces what you owe. Get the DIRECTION right and the arithmetic is easy; get it backwards and every number is wrong.
traps: Rent and prepaid taxes move in OPPOSITE directions. Ask who holds the cash.
Security deposits transfer to the buyer, not back to the tenant.
Origination and points are on the LOAN; commission and transfer tax are on the PRICE.

An amount reducing what a party owes.
Dividing a shared expense between the parties by time.
Paid after the period it covers, like Georgia property taxes.
Paid before the period it covers, like an annual insurance premium.

comp/situational.blurb: You are the licensee -- what do you actually do?

examples.k: Explain it must be disclosed. If the seller refuses, withdraw from the engagement.
examples.s: The seller tells you the HVAC failed last winter and was patched, then says 'don't put that on the disclosure.'
examples.t: The seller wants it off the form
w: A failed major system is a material fact.
You never complete or alter the seller's form.
You also cannot market the property knowing the disclosure is false.

examples.k: Do nothing with the money until a court or the agreed process decides.
examples.s: A closing fails. Buyer and seller each demand the $10,000 earnest money.
examples.t: Two people want the same deposit
w: The broker is a stakeholder, not a judge.
Releasing to either side, splitting it, or keeping it all invite a conversion claim.
Hold the funds and use interpleader or the prescribed procedure.

ga: In Georgia, trust funds must be deposited PROMPTLY unless ALL parties give written authority otherwise - the buyer's request alone is never enough.
Georgia protects nondisclosure of a death on the property, but never an outright denial.
comp/situational.label: Situational judgment

choices: Refuse, and withdraw if they persist
check.q: A client asks you to do something unlawful. You:
check.why: Referring relocates the violation.

choices: Keep it confidential for your client
check.q: You know a material fact about the property. You:
check.why: Confidentiality never covers a defect.

l: 1. Is anyone asking me to break the law or a fair housing rule? Refuse, and withdraw if they persist. Referring them to a colleague relocates the violation.
2. Do I know a MATERIAL FACT about the property? Disclose it. Confidentiality never covers a defect.
3. Am I about to state something I know is untrue? Decline instead. Declining is not deceit; inventing an answer is.
4. Is this money that belongs to someone else? Into the trust account promptly, and never choose between competing claimants.
5. Is this person a client or a customer? Clients get advice and advocacy; customers get honesty and material-defect disclosure.
6. Do I have a personal interest? Disclose it in writing before the offer is considered.

choices: Loan fraud if concealed from the lender
check.q: A buyer wants the price inflated with cash back at closing. This is:
check.why: The licensee who writes it participates.

check.q: You spot an error on the settlement statement. You:
check.why: Post-closing corrections are far harder.

l: A client gives a discriminatory instruction - refuse; withdraw if they persist.
A seller says 'leave it off the disclosure' - explain it must be disclosed; if they refuse, end the engagement. Never complete the form for them.
A buyer asks you to inflate the price with cash back at closing - that is loan fraud if concealed from the lender. Refuse.
You spot an error on the settlement statement - raise it BEFORE anyone signs.
You realise after closing that you miscalculated and your client overpaid - tell them; the duty to account survives closing.
An unrepresented buyer asks 'should I offer less?' - clarify that you represent the seller and suggest they get their own representation.
A colleague's licence has expired and they want cover - refuse and tell your broker; unlicensed activity is charged against the firm too.
A buyer waives inspection - document your recommendation in writing and still disclose what you observe.

You are paid a referral fee by an inspector - disclose it, or better, offer several names and take no fee. In a federally related mortgage transaction a referral fee for settlement services violates RESPA outright.

choices: May share it - it is public record
check.q: A past client asks the neighbour's recorded sale price. You:
check.why: Confidentiality covers motivation and position, not public facts.

p: It covers your client's motivation, finances, and negotiating position. It does NOT cover material defects, and it does not cover facts already in the public record - a closed sale price is public, and refusing to state it is unhelpfulness, not duty.

comp/situational.summary: These give you a scene and ask what you actually do. Four principles resolve almost all of them: never lie, never conceal a known defect, never act on an unlawful instruction, and never pick a side with money you are holding in trust.
traps: Referring a discriminating client to a colleague is not a solution.
'I didn't say anything untrue' is no defence to concealing a known defect.
Uniform application does not save a policy that is itself unlawful.
vocab: Anything affecting value, desirability, or the decision to buy.
Actively hiding a known material defect.
A personal stake that could compromise your duty to a client.
Depositing disputed funds with a court to decide.
Bans anything of value for referring settlement business.
A clerical, non-discretionary service for a customer.

comp/vocabulary.blurb: The terms both portions assume you already know.

examples.k: Encumbrance. If the stem had said 'a fence built two feet over the line', the answer would narrow to encroachment.
examples.s: 'A charge or claim against property that does not prevent transfer but travels with it.'
w: 'Travels with it' points to something running with the land.
'Does not prevent transfer' rules out anything blocking conveyance.
That is the general category, not the specific physical case.

ga: Georgia edition of the loan documents: the NOTE is the promise, the SECURITY DEED is the pledge - not a mortgage and not a deed of trust.
comp/vocabulary.label: Vocabulary & terminology

check.q: Which is a physical intrusion onto another's land?
check.why: Every encroachment is an encumbrance; not every encumbrance is physical.

check.q: In 'mortgagor' and 'mortgagee', the borrower is the:
check.why: The '-or' gives, the '-ee' receives.

l: Encumbrance / encroachment - any claim on the fee / a physical intrusion. Every encroachment is an encumbrance; not every encumbrance is physical.
Mortgagor / mortgagee - borrower / lender. The '-or' gives, the '-ee' receives. Same for lessor/lessee, vendor/vendee, optionor/optionee, grantor/grantee.
Acceleration / alienation - due on DEFAULT / due on TRANSFER.
Subrogation / subordination / substitution / satisfaction - stepping into another's claim / lowering lien priority / an equal alternative / recorded proof of payoff.
Assemblage / plottage - the ACT of combining parcels / the added VALUE that results.
Progression / regression - pulled up by better neighbours / dragged down by worse.
Accretion / erosion / avulsion / reliction - gradual gain / gradual loss / sudden change (boundaries do NOT move) / land exposed by receding water.
Executed / executory - fully performed / signed but not yet performed.
Void / voidable - never a contract / valid until the protected party disaffirms.
Latent / patent - hidden / obvious.
Riparian / littoral - flowing water / still water.
Fixture / trade fixture - conveys with the realty / stays the commercial tenant's.
Security deposit / prepaid rent - held in trust for the tenant / earned by the landlord.
Equitable / statutory right of redemption - before the sale / after the sale.

check.q: An opinion of the most probable price is:
check.why: Price is what it actually sold for.

l: Market value - an OPINION of most probable price.
Market price - the FACT of what it sold for.
Cost - what it took to build.
Assessed value - the tax base.
Insurable value - improvements only.

check.q: What comes immediately after net operating income?
check.why: Debt service is never an operating expense.

l: Potential gross income
- vacancy and collection loss = EFFECTIVE GROSS INCOME
- operating expenses = NET OPERATING INCOME
- debt service = CASH FLOW
Debt service is never an operating expense.

check.q: A judgment lien is:
check.why: A mortgage is specific and voluntary.

sections.h: Lien classifications are three independent axes
l: General (all property) vs. SPECIFIC (one parcel)
Voluntary (you agreed) vs. INVOLUNTARY (imposed)
Statutory (created by law) vs. EQUITABLE (created by fairness)
A judgment lien is general, involuntary, statutory. A mortgage is specific and voluntary. A question can test any axis.

check.q: Which renews automatically until notice?
check.why: An estate for years ends on its own with no notice.

l: Estate for years - fixed start and end, no notice needed
Periodic - renews until notice
At will - endable at either party's pleasure
At sufferance - holdover with no right

check.q: Which step actually passes title?
check.why: Notarisation is for recording; recording is for notice.

l: Execution (signing) -> Acknowledgment (notary, needed to RECORD) -> DELIVERY AND ACCEPTANCE (what passes title) -> Recording (constructive notice, priority)

check.q: Which power regulates without paying?
check.why: Only eminent domain requires just compensation.

l: Police power - regulate, no payment
Eminent domain - take, with just compensation
Taxation
Escheat - to the state when there is no will and no heir

traps: '-or' gives, '-ee' receives. Apply it to every pair.
Executed means fully PERFORMED in exam language, not merely signed.
Avulsion is sudden and does not move boundaries.

A physical intrusion onto another's land.
One party stepping into another's legal claim, typical of insurers.
The recorded document proving a debt is paid.
The added value created by assemblage.
Land exposed by permanently receding water.
The unbroken effort that produced a ready, willing and able buyer.
The right to cure default BEFORE the foreclosure sale.
A post-sale right to reclaim, where a state grants one.
Annual crops; the tenant-farmer's personal property.
Substituting a party and releasing the original.

w: BRRETA defines agency as representation by WRITTEN authority.
With no brokerage engagement there is no agency relationship.
But the licensee has behaved far outside the customer role.

examples.s: A broker assigns one licensee to the buyer and another to the seller in the same deal.

w: Each designated agent owes their own client the full statutory duties.

georgia/brreta.label: Brokerage relationships (BRRETA)

check.q: Under BRRETA, agency requires:
check.why: The brokerage engagement is a written contract.

check.q: A person NOT represented, for whom you may perform ministerial acts, is a:
check.why: Ministerial acts require no discretion.

l: AGENCY - every relationship in which a broker acts for or represents another as a CLIENT by that person's WRITTEN authority.
BROKERAGE ENGAGEMENT - the written contract by which a seller, buyer, landlord or tenant becomes the broker's client.
CLIENT - a person represented under a brokerage engagement.
CUSTOMER - a person NOT represented, for whom the broker may perform MINISTERIAL ACTS under either a verbal or written agreement.
MINISTERIAL ACTS - acts that do not require discretion or the exercise of the broker's own judgement.

check.q: Under BRRETA a Georgia broker is:
check.why: The broker owes reasonable care in the duties the statute and engagement specify.

check.q: A broker's duties may be expanded beyond the statute only by:

p: O.C.G.A. 10-6A-4(a): a broker owes a client or customer ONLY the duties set out in the chapter, unless the parties expressly agree otherwise in a signed writing. A broker SHALL NOT BE DEEMED to have a fiduciary relationship with any party, and is responsible only for exercising REASONABLE CARE in discharging the specified duties. Georgia deliberately narrowed common-law fiduciary exposure.

check.q: A seller pays the buyer's broker. That broker represents:
check.why: Compensation and agency are independent under BRRETA.

check.q: What creates the engagement?
check.why: Only the writing.

p: Paying the commission does not make you the payer's client. A seller paying the buyer's broker out of closing proceeds does not make that broker the seller's agent. Only an express written agreement creates the engagement. This is heavily tested because intuition runs the other way.

choices: That the broker represents other buyers generally
check.q: Which need NOT be disclosed before an engagement?
check.why: The statute expressly excludes it.

check.q: How many pre-engagement disclosures does BRRETA list?
check.why: Agency types, conflicts known, compensation, confidentiality.

sections.h: Disclosures before or within the engagement
l: The types of agency relationships available through the broker

Any brokerage relationships the broker holds with other parties that would CONFLICT with the prospective client's interests and are actually known - but EXPRESSLY EXCLUDING the fact that the broker may represent other sellers or landlords, or other buyers or tenants, generally
The broker's compensation and whether it will be shared with other brokers
The broker's obligations to keep information confidential
BRRETA does not require the agency conversation before the engagement, but the InfoBase urges having it as early as possible so a customer never presumes they are represented.
p: Before entering into a brokerage engagement, the broker must advise the prospective client of FOUR things:

check.q: A Georgia brokerage engagement must have:
check.why: Automatic renewals are prohibited.

check.q: An engagement with no end date is:
check.why: Disciplinary matter for the broker.

p: The engagement begins when the client engages the broker and runs until the agreed expiration date or another statutory ending event. GREC requires a DEFINITE expiration date, and automatic renewal clauses are prohibited.

check.q: Dual agency in Georgia is:
check.why: Consent is presumed if the writing contains the required elements.

check.q: A dual agent must disclose:
check.why: Never information a client asked be kept confidential.

l: A description of the transactions or types of transactions involved
A statement that the broker represents two clients whose interests are, or at times could be, different or even adverse
A statement that the dual agent will disclose all ADVERSE MATERIAL FACTS actually known - EXCEPT information made confidential by a client's request or instruction
A statement that the client does NOT have to consent to the dual agency
A statement that the consent has been given voluntarily and the writing has been read and understood
The practical rule: a dual agent discloses adverse material FACTS, never a client's negotiating POSITION.
p: A DUAL AGENT is a broker who simultaneously has a client relationship with both sides of the same transaction. Georgia ALLOWS it with WRITTEN consent. Consent is presumed where the writing contains:

check.q: With designated agents appointed, the broker is:
check.why: O.C.G.A. 10-6A-13(b) says neither the broker, the licensees, nor the firm.

check.q: A designated agent may share confidential client information with:
check.why: And the broker may not reveal it either.

sections.h: Designated agency - a genuine Georgia distinction
l: 10-6A-13(b): where designated agents are appointed, NEITHER the broker, NOR the broker's licensees, NOR the firm is deemed a dual agent. Many other states treat this as firm-wide dual agency; Georgia does not.
10-6A-13(c): there is NO IMPUTATION of knowledge between broker, designated agents, and clients - each is treated as having only their own actual knowledge.
A designated agent may not disclose confidential client information except to their BROKER, and the broker in turn may not reveal it.
Confidential information means anything whose disclosure the client has not consented to that could harm the client's negotiating position.
p: A broker may assign different affiliated licensees as DESIGNATED AGENTS to represent opposing clients in the same transaction, directly or through company policy. Each designated agent owes their own client the full statutory duties.

georgia/brreta.summary: BRRETA (the Brokerage Relationships in Real Estate Transactions Act, O.C.G.A. Title 10 Chapter 6A) is the single biggest difference between Georgia and general agency law. It was passed because licensees kept creating ACCIDENTAL agency by treating customers like clients. Its answer: agency requires WRITING, and duties are limited to what the statute and the engagement specify.
traps: Compensation never creates agency in Georgia.
A broker is expressly NOT a fiduciary under BRRETA - only reasonable care in specified duties.
Designated agency does NOT make the broker a dual agent.
The four pre-engagement disclosures exclude having to reveal other buyer/seller clients.

A represented party under a brokerage engagement.
An unrepresented party for whom ministerial acts may be performed.
Acts requiring no discretion or judgement by the broker.
A broker with client relationships on both sides of one transaction.
A licensee assigned to represent one client exclusively in a transaction.
A known fact that would materially affect the transaction.
Information a client has not consented to disclose that could harm their position.
Attributing one person's knowledge to another; removed for designated agency.

georgia/contracts.label: Georgia contracts & forms

choices: Acceptance is communicated to the offeror
check.q: A Georgia contract becomes binding when:
check.why: All deadlines run from that date.

choices: Any time before acceptance is communicated
check.q: An offer may be revoked:
check.why: After that, withdrawal is a breach.

p: A Georgia contract becomes binding when ACCEPTANCE IS COMMUNICATED to the offeror - not when the seller signs. Every subsequent deadline (due diligence, financing, closing) is measured from that BINDING AGREEMENT DATE, so getting it wrong shifts the whole timeline. An offer may be revoked any time before acceptance is communicated.

choices: For any reason, recovering the earnest money
check.q: During the due diligence period a Georgia buyer may typically terminate:
check.why: After it expires, the exits narrow sharply.

check.q: The due diligence period is measured from the:
check.why: Which is why getting that date right matters.

p: Georgia's standard due diligence provision gives the buyer a set number of days to inspect and, under the common forms, to TERMINATE FOR ANY REASON OR NO REASON and recover the earnest money. That latitude is why the length is negotiated hard. Once it expires the buyer's exit rights narrow sharply and the earnest money is genuinely at risk.

choices: Fill in blanks on approved preprinted forms
check.q: A Georgia licensee may:
check.why: Drafting is the unauthorised practice of law.

check.q: A typed special stipulation conflicting with preprinted text:
check.why: Specific terms beat boilerplate - which is why sloppy ones are dangerous.

l: A licensee MAY complete the blanks on approved preprinted forms incident to a transaction they are handling.
A licensee MAY NOT draft original clauses or give legal advice about them - that is the unauthorised practice of law.

Handwritten or typed SPECIAL STIPULATIONS PREVAIL over conflicting preprinted text, because they show the parties' specific intent. That is exactly why a badly drafted stipulation is dangerous: it controls the deal.
Complex terms - owner financing, unusual contingencies - belong with an attorney.

choices: Identify the property with reasonable certainty
check.q: A Georgia contract's property description must:
check.why: A vague description can make it unenforceable.

p: Georgia courts require a description that identifies the property with reasonable certainty, or provides a 'key' leading to identification. A vague description can make the contract unenforceable for indefiniteness.

choices: Be in writing with a definite expiration date
check.q: A Georgia listing agreement must:
check.why: Automatic renewals are prohibited.

l: Must be IN WRITING with a DEFINITE EXPIRATION DATE.
AUTOMATIC RENEWAL clauses are prohibited - a broker cannot roll a listing forward by default.
An engagement with no ending date is a licence-law violation for the broker, separate from whether the client minds.

choices: Be a reasonable pre-estimate of loss
Be at least 10% of the price
check.q: For a liquidated damages clause to be enforceable it must:
check.why: A sum operating as a penalty is void.

p: Where the contract provides liquidated damages, the seller normally retains the earnest money as the agreed measure of loss. To be enforceable rather than a penalty it must be a reasonable pre-estimate of damages, damages must be hard to determine, and the parties must have intended it as liquidated damages.

choices: Keep marketing while a buyer's sale contingency is pending

check.q: A licensee who sees a fresh paint patch over a stain should:

check.q: Georgia protects a licensee who:

check.q: Asked directly whether someone died there, the safest answer is to:
check.why: Declining keeps you inside the protection.

check.q: Georgia's property disclosure statement is completed by the:
check.why: Filling it in for them transfers their liability to you.

choices: Not pass it along, and withdraw if the seller refuses to correct it
Disclose only to the buyer's agent
check.q: If a licensee knows an answer on the form is false, they must:

p: The SELLER completes Georgia's property disclosure statement from personal knowledge. A licensee should never complete it for the seller or guess at answers - doing so transfers the seller's liability onto the licensee. If the licensee knows an answer is false, they cannot market the property on that basis; if the seller will not correct it, withdraw.

check.q: Which must be disclosed?
check.why: Physical conditions affecting value, safety, or use.

check.q: Flood plain location is:
check.why: It affects value, insurability, and use.

l: Known physical defects affecting value, safety, or use - roof, foundation, septic, systems, water intrusion (including repaired history)
Flood plain location, which affects value, insurability, and lender requirements
Federal lead-based paint disclosure for housing built before 1978, with records, the EPA pamphlet, and a 10-day testing opportunity
A licensee's own LICENSED STATUS, in writing, whenever acting as a principal

choices: Protected - handicap is a protected class
check.q: A former occupant's HIV status is:
check.why: Disclosure would be discriminatory.

p: Anything touching a protected class. A former occupant's HIV/AIDS status is protected as handicap; the demographic makeup of a neighbourhood is off limits because answering steers.

georgia/disclosures.summary: Georgia's disclosure rules are narrower than most states'. The duty is to adverse material facts ACTUALLY KNOWN - there is no duty to investigate - and Georgia expressly protects licensees who stay silent about stigma. What is never protected is an affirmative lie.
traps: Physical condition must be disclosed; stigma generally need not.
The duty covers what you ACTUALLY KNOW - but it runs to customers too.
Never complete the seller's disclosure form for them.

The seller's written statement of known conditions.

examples.s: A licensee provides school ratings and crime statistics only when buyers of a certain background ask for them.
w: Nothing negative was said about any area.
But information was delivered selectively by who was asking.
Selective information channels buyers just as effectively as a recommendation.

Waiving the pet policy is a reasonable ACCOMMODATION at the provider's expense.
Charging a fee defeats the accommodation.

georgia/fair-housing.label: Fair housing in Georgia

check.q: Which is federally protected in housing?
check.why: Source of income and marital status are not among the seven.

p: Race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, handicap. Source of income and marital status are not among them federally, though some Georgia local ordinances protect source of income and a blanket policy can still create disparate-impact exposure.

check.q: Giving school ratings only to certain buyers is:
check.why: Selective information channels buyers just as effectively.

check.q: An ad saying 'no children under 12' violates:
check.why: Describe the property, not the occupant.

l: STEERING does not require saying anything negative. Providing school ratings and crime statistics only to certain buyers, or 'you'd be more comfortable over here', both steer. Use a consistent policy for every buyer and point everyone to the same public sources.
BLOCKBUSTING is inducing sales by suggesting a protected group's arrival will harm the neighbourhood. Illegal whether or not the statement is true.
Advertising must describe the PROPERTY, not the desired occupant. 'Mature Christian couple' signals age/familial status and religion; 'no children under 12' is a direct familial status violation.

check.q: A tenant wants to install a grab bar. This is a:
check.why: Physical change = modification.

check.q: Charging a pet fee for an assistance animal is:
check.why: An assistance animal is not a pet.

l: REASONABLE MODIFICATION - a PHYSICAL change (grab bar, ramp, doorbell light). Permitted at the TENANT'S expense, with possible restoration on move-out.
REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION - a change to RULES or policies (waiving a no-pets rule for an assistance animal). At the HOUSING PROVIDER'S expense.
An assistance animal is not a pet: no pet fee or pet deposit may be charged, though the tenant remains liable for actual damage.

choices: Refuse and withdraw if they persist
check.q: A seller insists you exclude a protected class. You should:
check.why: Referring simply relocates the violation.

p: The duty of obedience covers LAWFUL instructions only. A seller who directs you to exclude a protected class must be refused, and if they persist you WITHDRAW. Quietly ignoring the instruction leaves you working for someone who will discriminate; handing the seller to a colleague simply relocates the violation.

choices: A HUD case, a lawsuit, and GREC discipline
check.q: One discriminatory act can result in:
check.why: The tracks are independent.

p: HUD handles federal complaints, generally within one year. Private suits are available. Separately, GREC can discipline the licence - so one act of discrimination can produce a HUD case, a lawsuit, and a licence sanction.

georgia/fair-housing.summary: Georgia enforces the federal Fair Housing Act, and GREC can independently discipline a licensee for discriminatory conduct. The exam focuses on recognising steering and blockbusting in realistic wording, and on the accommodation/modification split.
traps: Steering can happen through selective helpfulness, with no negative statement at all.
Modification = physical = tenant pays. Accommodation = rules = provider absorbs.
Refusing an unlawful instruction is not enough if you keep the listing - withdraw.
vocab: The federal law barring housing discrimination on seven grounds.
Households with children under 18, pregnant people, those securing custody.
Disability, including HIV/AIDS; a protected class.
Channelling people toward or away from areas by protected class.
Inducing sales with claims about a protected group moving in.
Refusing or pricing loans by area demographics.
A physical change at the tenant's expense.
A rules change at the provider's expense.
Not a pet; no pet fee may be charged.
A neutral policy with discriminatory effect.
The narrow exemption from familial status protection.

examples.s: A salesperson licensed 14 months ago never took the 25-hour postlicense course, but did complete some CE.
w: The postlicense course is due within ONE year of original licensure.

examples.k: Discipline and compensation are separate tracks. Do not wait for the investigation before consulting an attorney.
examples.s: A consumer loses $18,000 through a licensee's mishandling of funds and files a complaint with GREC.
w: GREC may reprimand, suspend, revoke, fine, and require education or CPA reports.
It has no authority to order repayment of a financial loss.
The consumer must pursue a civil action for the money.

georgia/license-law.label: GREC license law & rules

check.q: The Georgia salesperson prelicense course is:
check.why: 60 hours is the broker course; 25 is postlicense.

choices: Three of the past five years
check.q: Experience required for a salesperson licence:
check.why: The three-of-five rule is for broker and associate broker.

l: AGE - 18 for salesperson or community association manager; 21 for broker or associate broker. You may TAKE the salesperson exam at 17 but cannot activate until 18 (and the broker exam at 20, activating at 21).
EDUCATION - a 75-HOUR GREC-approved salesperson prelicense course. Brokers take a 60-hour broker prelicense course.
EXAMINATION - pass the Georgia licensing exam (national + state portions).

EXPERIENCE - NONE for a salesperson. For broker or associate broker, an ACTIVE licence for THREE of the FIVE years immediately preceding application. Active licensure in ANOTHER state counts, with a certified licence history from every state where you have held one.
Background check and application fee.

check.q: The 25-hour postlicense course is due within:
check.why: Miss it and the licence lapses. CE does not substitute.

check.q: Georgia continuing education is:
check.why: Many national guides quote 36 - that is a different state.

l: POSTLICENSE - a 25-hour Sales Post-license Course within ONE YEAR of original licensure. Applies whether you are active or inactive, resident or nonresident. Miss it and the licence lapses. CE does not substitute for it.
CONTINUING EDUCATION - at least 24 HOURS of GREC-approved CE during each FOUR-YEAR renewal period. Not annual. Many national guides say 36 hours; that is a different state.
The sequence to remember: 75 in, 25 in year one, then 24 every four years.

check.q: An inactive Georgia licensee:
check.why: Fees and postlicense still apply; licensed activity does not.

check.q: A Georgia salesperson may be paid by:
check.why: Direct payment from a client is a violation.

l: INACTIVE status - you may hold a licence without affiliating, but you still pay fees and still owe the postlicense requirement. You may not perform licensed acts.
Change of address, broker affiliation, or status is made by filing a CHANGE APPLICATION with the Commission.
A salesperson acts only through and under the supervision of their affiliated broker, and may be COMPENSATED ONLY BY THAT BROKER.
NONRESIDENTS who hold no licence at home must meet the same requirements as Georgia residents and affiliate with a GREC-licensed broker, who may themselves be resident or nonresident.
Criminal CONVICTIONS must be reported to GREC. Concealment is usually punished more severely than the underlying offence.

choices: An independent violation by the broker
check.q: Failure to supervise an affiliate is:
check.why: GREC can act on its own motion.

check.q: Georgia advertising must:
check.why: A licensee may never appear to operate independently.

sections.h: The qualifying broker and the firm
l: The qualifying broker answers to GREC for the firm's compliance: supervision, trust accounts, records, and advertising.
FAILURE TO SUPERVISE is an independent violation - the broker can be disciplined for an affiliate's conduct.

If a qualifying broker is suspended, a corporation or LLC may keep operating if it IMMEDIATELY designates a replacement; otherwise the firm's licence and all affiliated licences are suspended for the same period.
Advertising must identify the FIRM and must never suggest a licensee operates independently of their broker.

choices: Order a licensee to repay a consumer's loss
check.q: GREC can do all of these EXCEPT:
check.why: There is no restitution power - the consumer must sue.

check.q: GREC members are:
check.why: Gubernatorial appointment.

sections.h: What GREC can do - and what it cannot
l: Members are appointed by the GOVERNOR. GREC administers the licence law, makes rules, investigates, and disciplines.
SANCTIONS: reprimand, suspension, revocation, fines, required education, and required reports from an independent accountant on the trust account.
GREC CANNOT order a licensee to repay a consumer's financial loss. There is no restitution power. A wronged consumer must sue civilly and should not wait for the investigation to conclude.
GREC also does NOT resolve commission disputes between brokers - those go to arbitration or the courts.

choices: Anyone by sworn written request, or the Commission itself
Only a party to the transaction
check.q: A GREC investigation may be started by:
check.why: It can also act on its own motion.

check.q: After an ALJ decision, the respondent has how long to seek Commission review?
check.why: Otherwise the decision becomes final.

l: ANYONE may file a sworn written request for investigation, and the Commission may act ON ITS OWN MOTION. The licensee is notified they are under investigation.

Where a violation caused no significant public harm, GREC may offer a CONSENT ORDER stating the violation and a proposed sanction. The licensee may sign, propose an alternative, present evidence, or demand a hearing.
A CONSENT SETTLEMENT fixes agreed findings of fact, conclusions of law, and a sanction, with no hearing held.
A formal hearing is conducted by an ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGE from the Office of State Administrative Hearings.

The respondent has THIRTY DAYS to ask the Commission to review the ALJ's decision; otherwise it becomes final. The Commission has the same 30 days to request review. From the Commission's final decision, appeal goes to the courts.
Commission staff may not interpret the law for you - that is legal advice.

check.q: A licensee selling their own home must:
check.why: O.C.G.A. 43-40-29(c) removes the ordinary-owner exemptions.

check.q: Net listings in Georgia are:
check.why: They create a direct conflict with the client's interest.

sections.h: A licensee is never an ordinary owner
p: O.C.G.A. 43-40-29(c) provides that NONE of the exceptions to licensure applies to a person who holds a licence. Selling or leasing your own property means disclosing your licensed status IN WRITING in the contract or lease, and placing any trust funds in an account approved by your broker. Georgia also permits NET LISTINGS only under strict disclosure conditions.

georgia/license-law.summary: The biggest single block on the state portion (14 questions). Three clusters carry most of it: what you must do to GET and KEEP a licence, what GREC can and cannot do to you, and the fact that being a licensee never lets you act as an ordinary owner.
traps: 75 prelicense / 25 postlicense - candidates transpose these constantly.
CE is 24 hours per FOUR YEARS, not per year and not 36.
GREC cannot order restitution, and does not settle commission disputes.
Being a licensee removes, not grants, the ordinary-owner exemptions.
vocab: The Georgia Real Estate Commission; members appointed by the Governor.
The broker responsible to GREC for a firm's compliance.
A broker-licensed individual working under a qualifying broker.
25 hours due within one year of original licensure.
Holding a licence without affiliating; no licensed activity permitted.
The GREC form used to report affiliation or status changes.
A negotiated resolution stating the violation and sanction, no hearing.
Agreed findings, conclusions and sanction without a hearing.
The OSAH officer who conducts formal GREC hearings.
Broker keeps everything above the seller's stated net; strictly limited in Georgia.

georgia/procedures.blurb: Attorney-conducted closings, title, transfer tax, recording.

examples.k: Say plainly that the attorney represents the lender and the buyer may retain their own counsel. Letting the buyer assume otherwise is a costly misunderstanding.
examples.s: At closing the buyer asks the attorney whether the repair clause protects them.
examples.t: Who does the closing attorney work for?
w: Georgia requires attorney supervision of the closing.
That attorney customarily represents the LENDER, not the buyer.
The licensee must not supply a legal opinion either.

examples.k: The claim is complete. Without colour of title they would have needed 20 years.
examples.s: A neighbour has openly occupied a strip of land for 12 years under a deed they believed valid but which was defective.
w: A defective instrument that appears to convey title is COLOUR OF TITLE.
With colour of title Georgia's period is 7 years, not 20.
Twelve years exceeds it.

georgia/procedures.label: Closings, escrow & procedure

check.q: A Georgia closing must be supervised by:
check.why: Examining title and preparing documents is the practice of law.

check.q: The closing attorney customarily represents:
check.why: A buyer wanting an advocate must retain their own counsel.

p: Georgia requires a licensed ATTORNEY to supervise the closing, because examining title and preparing conveyance documents is the practice of law. That attorney customarily represents the LENDER. A buyer who wants their own advocate must retain separate counsel - and a licensee should say so plainly rather than letting the buyer assume otherwise.

choices: Passes legal title to the lender until payoff
check.q: A Georgia security deed:
check.why: That makes Georgia a title-theory state.

p: Georgia's security instrument is a SECURITY DEED (deed to secure debt). Unlike a mortgage, which creates only a lien, it conveys LEGAL TITLE to the lender until the debt is paid. This is what makes Georgia a title-theory state and enables fast nonjudicial foreclosure.

choices: The first Tuesday of the month
The last Friday of the month
check.q: Georgia foreclosure sales occur on:
check.why: On the courthouse steps, after advertisement in the legal organ.

choices: Nonjudicial under a power of sale
check.q: Georgia foreclosure is:
check.why: Which is why it moves comparatively fast.

l: Georgia foreclosure is NONJUDICIAL, under the power of sale in the security deed.
Notice to the borrower, plus ADVERTISEMENT in the county LEGAL ORGAN, customarily for four weeks.
Public sale on the courthouse steps on the FIRST TUESDAY of the month.
A deficiency requires court confirmation of the sale.

check.q: Georgia's transfer tax is:
check.why: Customarily paid by the seller.

check.q: Georgia deeds are recorded with the:
check.why: In the county where the land lies.

l: Georgia real estate TRANSFER TAX is $1.00 per $1,000 of consideration (0.10%). Customarily paid by the SELLER.
Collected by the CLERK OF SUPERIOR COURT when the deed is recorded.
Deeds, security deeds, and plats are recorded with the clerk of superior court in the county where the land lies, giving constructive notice.
There is also an intangible recording tax on long-term notes.

check.q: Georgia property taxes become a lien on:
check.why: Which is why closings prorate them.

p: Georgia property taxes become a LIEN ON JANUARY 1 of the tax year and follow the property regardless of who owned it when they accrued. That is why closings prorate them. Unpaid taxes produce a SELLER DEBIT and BUYER CREDIT.

check.q: Georgia does NOT recognise:
check.why: Spouses use joint tenancy with right of survivorship instead.

check.q: Adverse possession without colour of title in Georgia takes:
check.why: 7 years applies WITH colour of title.

l: Georgia does NOT recognise tenancy by the entirety. Spouses wanting survivorship hold as JOINT TENANTS WITH RIGHT OF SURVIVORSHIP, stated expressly.
Adverse possession: 20 YEARS, or 7 YEARS under COLOUR OF TITLE.
Georgia subdivisions are usually described by LOT AND BLOCK from a recorded plat; Georgia does not use the rectangular survey system.

check.q: The Closing Disclosure must be received:
check.why: TRID applies in Georgia like everywhere else.

p: TRID applies: the Closing Disclosure must be received at least three business days before consummation. The closing attorney disburses, records, and issues title insurance.

georgia/procedures.summary: Closing and conveyancing in Georgia differ from the national norm in several specific ways, and the exam tests exactly those differences: attorney closings, security deeds, nonjudicial foreclosure, transfer tax, January 1 tax liens, and no tenancy by the entirety.
traps: Georgia is an attorney-closing state, not an escrow state.
Security deed, not mortgage; nonjudicial foreclosure, first Tuesday.
$1.00 per $1,000 - divide the price by 1,000. Not 1% and not $0.10.
Tax lien attaches January 1, regardless of when the bill arrives.
vocab: Georgia's instrument conveying title to the lender as security.
The doctrine that the lender holds legal title until the debt is paid.
The county newspaper designated for official legal advertisements.
Court approval required before pursuing a deficiency in Georgia.
$1.00 per $1,000 of consideration, customarily paid by the seller.
A Georgia tax on long-term notes secured by real estate.
The county officer with whom Georgia land records are filed.
A defective written instrument that appears to convey title.

examples.k: The buyer's verbal request is not enough. Get it in writing from everyone, normally as a stipulation in the offer.
examples.s: A buyer asks the broker to hold the earnest money check uncashed until the seller accepts.
examples.t: Holding a check needs everyone's signature
w: The default rule is prompt deposit into a non-interest-bearing account.
Any deviation requires clear WRITTEN authority.
It must be agreed by ALL parties - the seller has an interest in the deposit too.

examples.s: A client already has $250,000 at XYZ Bank and gives the broker a $10,000 deposit. The broker's trust account is also at XYZ. The bank fails.
w: Pass-through treats the client as a separate owner - but the FDIC AGGREGATES their deposits at that bank.
The client is at $260,000 total, so $10,000 is uninsured.
The InfoBase warns the broker may be liable for it if the bank was not disclosed.

choices: Do not become part of the estate

check.why: They are also protected from garnishment and bankruptcy.

l: Do NOT become part of the broker's estate on death
Are NOT subject to attachment or garnishment from a judgment against the broker

Are not available to accidentally cover shortfalls in the firm's operating account

check.q: A Georgia trust account should be opened under:
check.why: SSN-based accounts have been seized for the broker's personal debts.

check.q: The account must be designated as trust or escrow by:
check.why: And registered with the Commission.

l: A SEPARATE, FEDERALLY INSURED bank CHECKING account that the BANK designates as a trust or escrow account.
Registered with the Commission at the time of broker application, and the broker must have SIGNATORY POWER.
It may be interest-bearing or non-interest-bearing, but funds are deposited into a NON-interest-bearing account unless all parties authorise otherwise in writing.

Open it under an EMPLOYER IDENTIFICATION NUMBER, not the broker's Social Security Number. The InfoBase records accounts seized by the IRS for a broker's personal tax debt, awarded in a divorce, and attached by a bank - the common thread was an account opened under the broker's SSN.
A broker must have AT LEAST ONE and may have several - commonly separate accounts for earnest money, rents, and security deposits. Each must be bank-designated and registered.

check.q: To hold an earnest money check until acceptance, the broker needs:
check.why: The seller has an interest in the deposit too.

check.q: Trust funds are deposited by default into:
check.why: Interest-bearing requires written authorisation.

p: The law requires trust funds to be deposited PROMPTLY. To do anything else - hold a check until the offer is accepted, take a postdated check, accept personal property instead of money, or use an interest-bearing account - the broker needs CLEAR WRITTEN AUTHORITY agreed to by ALL parties, not just the one who asked. Once deposited, funds stay there until the transaction is consummated or terminated.

choices: Commission properly earned and disbursed after closing
check.q: Which is NOT trust money?
check.why: Once earned and disbursed it is the broker's.

check.q: A buyer's advance for a credit report is:
check.why: Funds advanced for expenses are held in trust.

l: Earnest money and other deposits
RENTS collected for an owner
SECURITY, damage, cleaning, key deposits, and last month's rent
Payments collected on land contracts or wraparound mortgages on licensee-owned property
Any funds advanced by a party for expenses - appraisals, credit reports, repairs
Closing funds the broker collects and disburses
NOT trust money: commission properly earned and disbursed after closing.

check.q: FDIC pass-through coverage treats each client as:
check.why: Provided the broker meets the recordkeeping rules.

choices: Has no coverage for their new deposit
check.q: A client with $250,000 already at the same bank:
check.why: The FDIC aggregates their deposits at that bank.

p: The FDIC insures $250,000 per account owner per bank. Trust accounts get PASS-THROUGH coverage - each buyer, seller, or tenant is treated as a separate owner - but only if the broker meets the recordkeeping requirements. The catch: the FDIC ADDS that person's other deposits at the SAME bank. A client already at $250,000 in that bank has no coverage for their deposit, and the InfoBase warns the broker may be liable for the uninsured excess if the client was not told which bank holds the funds.

check.q: GREC may examine a trust account:
check.why: It may accept a CPA certification instead, at its discretion.

check.q: An affiliate holding an account for their own rentals must provide:
check.why: And the broker registers it and stays responsible.

l: Written notice to GREC, on Commission forms, whenever the bank, account name, or account number changes, the bank changes names, or the account closes.
GREC may EXAMINE trust accounts on reasonable request and does so routinely. It MAY, at its discretion, accept a CPA's certification of compliance instead.
A nonresident broker may keep the account in their home state if they authorise GREC to examine it.

If a broker lets an affiliate maintain an account for the affiliate's own rentals, the broker must REGISTER it with GREC, remains RESPONSIBLE for it, and the affiliate must supply at least QUARTERLY written reconciliation statements comparing total trust liability with the reconciled bank balance.

choices: Release to the first to ask
check.q: Both parties demand the earnest money. The broker should:
check.why: Choosing a side invites a conversion claim.

p: When buyer and seller both demand the deposit, the broker must not choose a side. Hold the funds and use interpleader or the prescribed procedure. Releasing, splitting, or keeping it all invite a conversion claim.

georgia/trust-accounts.summary: Trust account rules exist to keep the public's money separate from the broker's, and they survive the broker's death, bankruptcy, divorce, and judgments. Nearly every question here is about separation, prompt deposit, or paperwork.

w: Obedience covers LAWFUL instructions only.
Familial status is a protected class under the Fair Housing Act.
Complying would make the agent personally liable alongside the seller.

ga: In Georgia, agency requires WRITTEN authority - a brokerage engagement. BRRETA also provides that a broker is NOT deemed a fiduciary; the broker owes reasonable care in the duties the statute and the engagement specify.
Paying a broker's commission does not by itself create agency in Georgia.
national/agency.label: Principles of agency

check.q: Which duties SURVIVE the end of the agency?
check.why: The other four end with the relationship.

check.q: The duty of obedience covers:
check.why: An unlawful instruction must be refused.

l: Obedience - follow LAWFUL instructions. You must refuse unlawful ones.
Loyalty - put the client's interests ahead of your own.
Disclosure - tell the client everything material you know.
Confidentiality - protect the client's private information. SURVIVES the end of the relationship, indefinitely.
Accounting - account for all money and documents. Also survives closing.
Reasonable care and diligence - competence and skill.
Which survive termination? CONFIDENTIALITY and ACCOUNTING. The rest end.

check.q: Agency created by conduct rather than agreement is:
check.why: This is the accidental-agency trap.

check.q: Which does NOT terminate an agency?
check.why: Refusing an offer is just the client exercising judgement.

sections.h: How agency is created and ended
l: Express - written or spoken agreement. Written is required in Georgia.
Implied - created by CONDUCT that leads someone to reasonably believe they are represented. This is the accidental-agency trap.
Ratification - approving an unauthorised act after the fact.
Estoppel - a party is barred from denying an agency their conduct created.

Termination: expiration, completion, mutual agreement, revocation, renunciation, death or incapacity of either party, destruction of the property, or bankruptcy. A client simply refusing an offer does NOT end the agency.

check.q: A listing broker is usually a:
check.why: Narrow authority for one transaction.

check.q: A property manager is usually a:
check.why: Ongoing authority across a range of matters.

l: Special agent - narrow authority for one transaction. The typical listing broker.
General agent - ongoing authority in a range of matters. A property manager.
Universal agent - may act in all matters, usually under power of attorney.

choices: Honesty and disclosure of known material defects
check.q: A customer is owed:
check.why: Advocacy and advice belong to clients.

check.q: A subagent owes fiduciary duties to:
check.why: A subagent works through the listing broker.

l: Client / principal - the represented party, owed full duties.
Customer - unrepresented; owed honesty, fair dealing, and disclosure of known material defects. NOT owed advice, advocacy, or confidentiality.
Subagent - works through the listing broker and owes duties to the SELLER, even while driving the buyer around all day.
Dual agent - represents both sides in the same transaction. Duties shrink to neutrality; requires informed written consent from both. Illegal in some states.
Designated agent - one licensee assigned to each side within the same firm.

check.q: Mixing client funds with the broker's own money is:
check.why: Spending them is conversion - worse.

check.q: 'The best view in town' is:
check.why: Exaggerated opinion is puffing; a false statement of fact is not.

l: Puffing vs. misrepresentation - exaggerated opinion ('best view in town') is puffing. A false statement of MATERIAL FACT is misrepresentation.
Confidentiality never covers a known material DEFECT. You may decline to state a seller's motivation; you may not lie about the roof.
Commingling - mixing client funds with the broker's own. CONVERSION is spending them - far worse.
Failure to present all offers. Every offer goes to the seller, including ones you dislike or that pay you less.
Undisclosed personal interest - a family or financial stake in a party must be disclosed in writing before the offer is considered.
Letting an unlicensed assistant discuss terms, negotiate, or hold an open house unaccompanied.

choices: Ready, willing and able on the seller's terms
check.q: Commission is classically earned when the broker produces a buyer who is:
check.why: Under most listings it is earned then, even if the seller refuses to close.

check.q: A dispute between two brokers over procuring cause is decided by:
check.why: Commissions are not a licence-law matter.

p: Classically, when the broker produces a buyer who is READY, WILLING, AND ABLE on the seller's stated terms. Under most modern listing agreements it is earned at that moment even if the seller then refuses to close. PROCURING CAUSE - the uninterrupted chain of events that produced the buyer - decides disputes between brokers, and is settled by arbitration or the courts, not the licensing commission.

national/agency.summary: Agency is about whose interests you are legally bound to advance. A CLIENT gets fiduciary-level duties; a CUSTOMER gets honesty and disclosure of known material defects. Most agency questions are really asking which one the person is.
traps: Confidentiality and accounting survive termination. Loyalty, obedience, disclosure and care do not.
A subagent works with the buyer but owes duties to the SELLER.
Refusing an offer does not terminate the agency.
Commingling is mixing; conversion is spending. Know which the question describes.
vocab: A relationship where one person acts for another with authority.
The represented party, owed full duties.
An unrepresented party owed honesty and material-defect disclosure.
One who holds a position of trust and must act in another's interest.
Obedience, Loyalty, Disclosure, Confidentiality, Accounting, Reasonable care.
Agency created by explicit written or spoken agreement.
Approving an unauthorised act after it occurred.
Being barred from denying an agency your conduct created.
Limited authority for a single transaction.
Ongoing authority across a range of matters.
Authority to act in all matters, typically by power of attorney.
An agent working through the listing broker, owing duties to the seller.
A broker representing both parties in one transaction.
A licensee assigned to represent one client exclusively within a firm.
Exaggerated opinion that is not a statement of fact.
A false statement of material fact.
Mixing client trust funds with the broker's own funds.
Spending or using client trust funds.
The uninterrupted effort that produced a ready, willing and able buyer.
A buyer prepared to purchase on the seller's terms.

national/contracts.blurb: Formation, contingencies, breach and remedies, assignment.

examples.k: No contract on the original terms. The buyer may accept the late acceptance as a fresh offer, or walk away.
examples.s: The offer says acceptance must be RECEIVED by 5pm Friday. The seller signs at 3pm Friday but the acceptance is not delivered until Saturday morning.
examples.t: Signed in time, delivered too late
w: Acceptance is effective on COMMUNICATION, not on signature.
Nothing was communicated before the deadline, so the offer lapsed.
The late acceptance is legally a new offer.

examples.k: The buyer prevails and recovers the earnest money.
examples.s: The contract is contingent on financing at no more than 6.5%. The buyer is approved at 6.75% and terminates. The seller cries bad faith.
w: The parties fixed a number, and 6.75% does not meet it.
Courts enforce the stated term; materiality is not re-argued afterwards.
The buyer only needed to apply in good faith, which one genuine application meets.

examples.k: Only a novation - substituting the party with the seller's consent - would release the original buyer.
examples.s: A buyer assigns her purchase contract to a third party. The contract is silent on assignment; the seller objects.
w: Real estate contracts are assignable unless they say otherwise.
The assignment is valid over the seller's objection.
But the original buyer remains SECONDARILY liable.

ga: Georgia measures deadlines from the BINDING AGREEMENT DATE - the date acceptance is communicated to the offeror.
Georgia's standard DUE DILIGENCE period lets the buyer terminate for any reason and recover the earnest money. After it expires the buyer's exits narrow sharply.
A Georgia licensee may fill in blanks on approved preprinted forms. Drafting original clauses is the unauthorised practice of law.
Handwritten or typed special stipulations PREVAIL over conflicting preprinted text.
national/contracts.label: Contracts

check.q: Which is NOT required for a valid contract?
check.why: A promise for a promise is consideration enough.

choices: In writing and signed by the party to be charged
check.q: The Statute of Frauds requires a real estate contract to be:
check.why: Writing and signature - not notarisation.

l: Competent parties - legal age and sound mind.
Mutual assent - a valid offer and an acceptance that mirrors it.
Consideration - something of value each way. A promise for a promise is enough, so earnest money is NOT what makes a contract valid.
Lawful object - a legal purpose.
For real estate, add the STATUTE OF FRAUDS: it must be in writing and signed by the party to be charged. Leases of a year or less are commonly exempt.

check.q: A minor's contract is:
check.why: The adult party remains bound.

check.q: A contract for an illegal purpose is:
check.why: It was never a contract at all.

l: VALID - meets all requirements and binds both.
VOID - never a contract at all (illegal purpose).
VOIDABLE - one party may disaffirm: a minor's contract (voidable by the MINOR, the adult stays bound), or one induced by fraud, duress, menace, undue influence, or mistake.
UNENFORCEABLE - looks valid but a court will not enforce it, e.g. an oral land contract barred by the Statute of Frauds.

check.q: Acceptance is effective when:
check.why: Signing alone is not acceptance.

check.q: Changing one term in an offer creates a:
check.why: A counteroffer rejects and replaces the original.

l: Acceptance is effective when COMMUNICATED to the offeror. Signing alone is not acceptance.
MIRROR-IMAGE RULE - any change to terms is a COUNTEROFFER, which REJECTS the original and makes the former offeree the new offeror.
An offer terminates by: revocation before acceptance, rejection, counteroffer, lapse of the stated time, death or incapacity, or destruction of the property.
Private intent is irrelevant. Telling a friend you will probably accept changes nothing.

check.q: An option is the classic example of a:
check.why: The optionee need not buy; the optionor must sell if they do.

check.q: A contract signed but not yet closed is:
check.why: Executed means fully performed.

l: Bilateral - a promise for a promise. The typical purchase contract.
Unilateral - a promise for an ACT. An OPTION is the classic example: the seller must sell if the optionee exercises, but the optionee need not buy.
Executory - signed but not yet fully performed (between contract and closing).
Executed - fully performed by both. Careful: 'executed' also loosely means 'signed' in everyday speech, and the exam exploits that.

check.q: A contingency for financing at no more than 6.5% is satisfied by approval at 6.75%?
check.why: Courts enforce the number the parties wrote.

check.q: A contingency is a:
check.why: The duty to perform does not arise until it is met or waived.

p: A contingency is a condition precedent - the duty to perform does not arise until it is satisfied or waived. Read them exactly as written: an approval at 6.75% does not satisfy a contingency for financing at no more than 6.5%. The buyer must still apply in good faith.

check.q: A court ordering the actual transfer of the property is:
check.why: Available because land is legally unique.

check.q: Correcting a wrong parcel number both parties agree was a typo is:
check.why: The court rewrites the document to match true intent.

l: Specific performance - a court orders the actual transfer. Available because every parcel of land is legally unique.

Liquidated damages - the parties agree in advance what the loss is, usually the earnest money. Enforceable only if it is a reasonable pre-estimate; if it is so large it functions as a penalty, courts void it.
Compensatory damages - actual proven loss.
Rescission - unwind the contract and restore both parties to their prior position.
Reformation - a court REWRITES the document to reflect what the parties actually agreed, used for scrivener's errors like a wrong parcel number.

check.q: After assigning a purchase contract, the original buyer is:
check.why: Only a novation releases them.

check.q: Real estate purchase contracts are:
check.why: Silence means assignable.

l: ASSIGNMENT transfers RIGHTS. Real estate purchase contracts are assignable unless they say otherwise. The assignor stays SECONDARILY liable.
NOVATION substitutes a new party with everyone's consent and RELEASES the original. Only novation ends liability.

check.q: In a land contract the seller keeps:
check.why: The buyer takes possession and equitable title.

choices: Lets you match an offer the owner receives
Sets a price and forces a sale
Is the same as an option
check.q: A right of first refusal:
check.why: It is weaker than an option - no fixed price, no forced sale.

l: Option - the optionee buys the RIGHT to decide, for option consideration that is usually nonrefundable. Once paid it is binding and not revocable; a recorded option binds later buyers with notice.
Land contract / contract for deed - the seller keeps LEGAL title while the buyer takes possession and EQUITABLE title, paying over time.
Lease option - a lease plus a right to buy.
Right of first refusal - the right to match an offer the owner receives; weaker than an option because it does not set a price or force a sale.

check.q: Without a 'time is of the essence' clause, courts allow:
check.why: The clause is what makes dates strict.

check.q: Under the Uniform Vendor and Purchaser Risk Act, risk of loss before closing is on the:
check.why: The older doctrine of equitable conversion put it on the buyer.

l: 'Time is of the essence' turns stated dates into hard deadlines. Without it, courts allow performance within a REASONABLE time.
Equitable conversion (older rule) put risk of loss on the BUYER from signing. The Uniform Vendor and Purchaser Risk Act reverses that, leaving risk with the SELLER until title or possession passes.

national/contracts.summary: Contracts is the biggest block on the national exam (13 questions). Nearly every question reduces to one of three things: was a contract formed, what happens when someone does not perform, and can the deal be handed to someone else.
traps: Earnest money is not consideration and not required for validity.
A minor's contract is voidable BY THE MINOR; the adult remains bound.
'Executed' means fully performed in exam language, not merely signed.
Assignment transfers rights but keeps you liable. Novation is the release.
vocab: Requires real estate contracts to be in writing and signed.
A valid offer met by a matching acceptance.
Something of value exchanged by each party.
Valid until the protected party disaffirms.
Apparently valid but a court will not enforce it.
Acceptance must match the offer exactly or it is a counteroffer.
A response changing terms; rejects and replaces the original offer.
A promise exchanged for a promise.
A promise exchanged for an act.
Signed but not yet fully performed.
A condition that must be met before performance is due.
A condition that must occur before a duty arises.
A court order compelling the actual transfer.
An amount agreed in advance as the measure of loss.
Unwinding a contract and restoring the parties.
Court correction of a document to reflect true intent.
Transfer of contract rights; assignor stays secondarily liable.
Substituting a party and releasing the original.
A paid right to buy on set terms within a set time.
The one who must sell / the one who may buy.
Seller keeps legal title; buyer holds equitable title and possession.
The buyer's interest after contracting but before closing.
The right to match an offer the owner receives.
A good-faith deposit; evidence of intent, not what makes the contract valid.
A clause making stated dates strictly binding.
The doctrine placing risk of loss on the buyer at signing.

national/disclosures.blurb: Material facts, latent defects, lead paint, environmental hazards.

examples.k: Disclose it. Silence here is the classic post-closing lawsuit.
examples.s: A seller fixed a chronic basement leak two years ago and it has not recurred. They ask whether it goes on the disclosure.
w: Water intrusion history affects value, insurability, and recurrence risk.
That makes it material even though it is currently fixed.
Disclosing the problem AND the repair protects the seller.

examples.k: Property facts are disclosable. Protected characteristics of people are not.
examples.s: A buyer asks whether a nearby group home houses people with disabilities.
examples.t: A question you should not answer
w: Handicap is a protected class.
Answering, even truthfully and helpfully, facilitates steering.
Decline, and point the buyer to public sources they can research.

ga: Georgia expressly protects licensees from liability for NOT disclosing that a property was the site of a death, homicide, suicide, or felony.
Under BRRETA the duty runs to adverse material facts ACTUALLY KNOWN - there is no duty to inspect or investigate. But the duty runs to customers as well as clients.
The seller completes Georgia's property disclosure statement from personal knowledge. A licensee should never fill it in for them.
national/disclosures.label: Property condition & disclosures

check.q: A hidden defect not discoverable by ordinary inspection is:
check.why: Known latent defects must be disclosed.

choices: Still material and must be disclosed
check.q: A basement leak repaired two years ago is:
check.why: History bears on recurrence and insurability.

l: Material fact - anything affecting value, desirability, or the decision to buy.
LATENT defect - hidden, not discoverable by ordinary inspection. Known latent defects MUST be disclosed, because the buyer cannot find them.
PATENT defect - obvious on reasonable inspection.
A past problem that was repaired is still material - a history of flooding bears on recurrence and insurability. Disclose the problem AND the repair.
No duty to DISCOVER, but no licence to IGNORE. A visible red flag you actually observe must be passed on.

choices: Decline - handicap is a protected class
check.q: A buyer asks whether a former occupant had AIDS. You:
check.why: Disclosing it would itself be discriminatory.

choices: Decline and refer them to public data
check.q: A buyer asks about the racial makeup of a neighbourhood. You should:
check.why: Answering steers, however well intentioned.

l: A former occupant's HIV/AIDS status or other disability - handicap is protected.
The racial, religious, or ethnic makeup of a neighbourhood - answering steers.
Refer buyers to public data sources they can research themselves.
p: Facts about occupants that touch a protected class are off limits, because disclosing them facilitates discrimination:

check.q: Stigma arises from:
check.why: A death, crime, or rumour - not condition.

check.q: Georgia's protection covers:
check.why: Nondisclosure is protected; an affirmative lie is not.

p: Stigma comes from events - a death, a crime, a rumour - not physical condition. Most states, including Georgia, do NOT require disclosure and expressly protect licensees from liability for staying silent. But protection covers NONDISCLOSURE, not an affirmative lie. If asked directly, decline rather than deny.

check.q: The lead rule applies to housing built before:
check.why: Pre-1978 target housing.

choices: Disclose known hazards and allow a 10-day test window
check.q: The seller must:
check.why: Sellers are never required to test.

l: Applies to target housing built BEFORE 1978.
Seller must disclose known lead hazards and provide any records.
Buyer gets the EPA pamphlet and a 10-DAY opportunity to test.
The seller is never required to TEST. 'No knowledge' is a valid answer on the form.

check.q: Asbestos is most dangerous when it is:
check.why: Friable means it crumbles and releases fibres.

choices: Strict, joint and several, and retroactive
check.q: CERCLA liability is:
check.why: An innocent current owner can be liable.

l: Radon - naturally occurring radioactive gas entering through foundation cracks; second leading cause of lung cancer. Fixed with sub-slab depressurisation.
Asbestos - dangerous when FRIABLE (crumbles and releases fibres). Often best ENCAPSULATED rather than removed, since bad removal increases exposure.
Lead - paint in pre-1978 housing, and older service pipes.
Underground storage tanks - leak into soil and groundwater.
Mould, formaldehyde, groundwater contamination, brownfields.

CERCLA / Superfund - liability is STRICT, JOINT AND SEVERAL, and RETROACTIVE. A current owner can be liable without fault. The INNOCENT LANDOWNER defence requires appropriate due diligence, such as a Phase I, BEFORE buying.
Phase I ESA - records, interviews, site visit, non-invasive. Phase II involves sampling and testing, and only follows if Phase I finds a concern.

choices: Before or at the time of the offer
check.q: Seller disclosure should reach the buyer:
check.why: Late delivery usually gives a right to rescind.

choices: Records, interviews and a site visit
check.q: A Phase I environmental assessment involves:
check.why: Sampling is Phase II, and only if Phase I finds a concern.

p: Disclosure must reach the buyer early enough to weigh it before committing - normally before or at the time of the offer. Delivery after a binding contract typically gives the buyer a right to rescind.

national/disclosures.summary: The rule is simple and the exceptions are what get tested: disclose known material facts about the PROPERTY; never disclose facts about the PEOPLE. Agents are not inspectors and have no duty to hunt for defects, but they cannot ignore what they see or repeat what they know to be false.
traps: External and stigma facts feel similar but are opposite: physical condition must be disclosed, stigma generally need not.
Nondisclosure protection never licenses an affirmative lie.
CERCLA liability can attach to an innocent current owner - fault is not required.
vocab: Anything affecting value, desirability, or the decision to buy.
A hidden defect not discoverable by ordinary inspection.
An obvious defect visible on reasonable inspection.
Property made undesirable by events rather than condition.
'Let the buyer beware' - largely displaced by disclosure duties.
Residential property built before 1978, covered by the lead rule.
Able to be crumbled by hand, releasing fibres into the air.
Sealing a hazard in place instead of removing it.
A naturally occurring radioactive gas that enters through the foundation.
Superfund; imposes strict, joint and several, retroactive cleanup liability.
A CERCLA defence requiring pre-purchase due diligence.
A non-invasive environmental review of records and site conditions.
Sampling and testing that follows a concerning Phase I.
A property whose redevelopment is complicated by contamination.
Actively hiding a known material defect.

national/financing.blurb: Loan types, points, amortization, TRID/RESPA, qualifying ratios.

examples.k: The seller-borrower owes the deficiency. Had the buyer ASSUMED, both would be liable - buyer primarily, seller secondarily - unless a novation released the seller.
examples.s: A buyer takes title 'subject to' the seller's existing loan, then defaults. Foreclosure leaves a $40,000 shortfall.
w: 'Subject to' means the buyer never promised to pay the note.
The buyer's only exposure was losing the property, which has happened.
The ORIGINAL borrower's promise is still outstanding.

examples.k: Buy the points only if you will hold the loan longer than about four years.
examples.s: 6.5% with no points, or 6.0% with 2 points on a $300,000 loan.
examples.t: Do the points pay for themselves?
w: Rate saving is 0.5% x $300,000 = $1,500 in the first year.
$6,000 / $1,500 = 4 years to break even.

examples.k: The buyer must cover the $10,000 gap on top of the normal down payment, and without a contingency has no automatic right to walk.
examples.s: Contract price $310,000; appraisal comes in at $300,000; the loan is 80% LTV. There is no appraisal contingency.
w: The lender lends on the LESSER figure: 80% x $300,000 = $240,000.
The buyer still owes the contract price of $310,000.

ga: Georgia uses a SECURITY DEED, which conveys legal title to the lender until the debt is paid. That is why Georgia foreclosures are NONJUDICIAL under a power of sale.
Georgia foreclosure: notice to the borrower plus advertisement in the county legal organ, customarily four weeks, then a public sale on the courthouse steps on the FIRST TUESDAY of the month.
national/financing.label: Financing

check.q: Which document is the borrower's promise to repay?
check.why: The note is the debt; the security instrument pledges the collateral.

check.q: Georgia's security instrument is a:
check.why: A security deed passes legal title to the lender until payoff.

l: Promissory note - the borrower's personal promise to repay. This is the debt.

Security instrument - pledges the property as collateral. A MORTGAGE creates a lien in most states. A DEED OF TRUST adds a third party, the TRUSTEE, who holds title for the lender and can sell without a lawsuit. GEORGIA uses a SECURITY DEED (deed to secure debt), which passes legal title to the lender until payoff.
Mortgagor = borrower. Mortgagee = lender. The '-or' gives, the '-ee' receives.

check.q: Which clause is triggered by a TRANSFER rather than a default?
check.why: Alienation is the due-on-sale clause.

check.q: The clause requiring the lender to release the lien on payoff is:
check.why: Defeasance defeats the lien when the debt is paid.

l: Acceleration - on DEFAULT the whole balance becomes due. A prerequisite to foreclosure.
Alienation (due-on-sale) - on TRANSFER the whole balance becomes due. Triggered by sale, not default.
Defeasance - requires the lender to release the lien when the debt is paid.
Subordination - voluntarily moves a lien to lower priority, so a construction lender can take first position.
Prepayment penalty - a charge for paying early.
Release (partial release) - in a blanket mortgage, frees individual lots as portions of the debt are paid.

choices: Taking title subject to the loan
check.q: Which arrangement leaves the buyer with NO personal liability?
check.why: 'Subject to' means the buyer risks only the property.

check.q: What releases the original borrower from liability?
check.why: Only a novation substitutes the party and releases the original.

l: ASSUMPTION - the buyer becomes PRIMARILY liable; the seller stays SECONDARILY liable until the lender grants a release.
NOVATION - the lender substitutes the new borrower and RELEASES the original. Only a novation frees the seller.
'SUBJECT TO' - the buyer takes title but accepts NO personal liability. On default the buyer loses the property; the ORIGINAL borrower still owes any deficiency.

check.q: A loan with level payments that leaves a balloon is:
check.why: Fully amortized retires the debt by maturity; a term loan is interest only.

check.q: In an amortized loan, over time the interest portion of each payment:
check.why: As principal is repaid, interest on the balance falls.

l: Fully amortized - level payments retire principal and interest by maturity.
Partially amortized - level payments leave a BALLOON at the end.
Term (straight) loan - interest only, principal due at the end.
In an amortized loan the INTEREST portion shrinks and the principal portion grows with each payment. Interest for one month = balance x annual rate / 12.

check.q: One discount point equals 1% of the:
check.why: Always the loan. This is the most common math error.

choices: The lesser of price and appraised value
check.q: LTV is based on:
check.why: Lenders lend on the lower figure.

l: One discount point = 1% of the LOAN AMOUNT, never the sale price.
Points are prepaid interest that raise the lender's YIELD, letting the borrower take a lower note rate. Roughly 8 points move the yield about 1%.
Origination fee compensates the lender for making the loan; also a % of the loan.
