LTV = loan / value, where value is the LESSER of sale price and appraised value.
Conventional loans above 80% LTV require PMI, which protects the LENDER. FHA carries MIP instead; VA carries a funding fee and no monthly mortgage insurance.

check.q: PMI protects:
check.why: Private mortgage insurance covers the lender's risk above 80% LTV.

check.q: An ARM's interest rate equals:
check.why: The margin is the lender's constant markup; the index moves.

l: Conventional - not government backed. Conforming loans meet Fannie/Freddie limits.
FHA - insured by FHA, low down payment, MIP required.
VA - guaranteed for eligible veterans, no down payment, funding fee. Entitlement stays committed until the loan is paid or another veteran substitutes theirs.
ARM - rate = INDEX + MARGIN, adjusted periodically with periodic and lifetime caps. The margin is the lender's constant markup; the index moves with the market.
Purchase-money mortgage - seller financing taken back at the sale.
Blanket - covers multiple parcels, with a release clause.
Package - includes personal property.
Open-end - lets the borrower re-borrow up to a limit.
Wraparound - a new loan wrapped around an existing one the seller keeps paying.
Construction loan - short term, paid out in draws.

check.q: The secondary mortgage market:
check.why: It provides liquidity so lenders can lend again.

check.q: A consumer applying for a mortgage deals with the:
check.why: Consumers never deal with the secondary market directly.

p: The PRIMARY market originates loans to consumers. The SECONDARY market - Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Ginnie Mae - BUYS existing loans, returning cash to lenders so they can lend again. Consumers never deal with the secondary market directly.

check.q: The Closing Disclosure must be received:
check.why: The Loan Estimate is the one tied to application.

choices: Payment for the mere referral of settlement business
check.q: RESPA Section 8 prohibits:
check.why: Fees for services actually performed are fine.

l: TILA / Regulation Z - discloses the cost of credit, including the APR, and governs trigger terms in advertising.
RESPA - governs settlement services. Section 8 bans paying or receiving anything of value for the mere REFERRAL of settlement business. Fees for services actually performed are fine.
TRID timing - Loan Estimate within 3 business days of APPLICATION; Closing Disclosure received at least 3 business days before CONSUMMATION.
Only three changes restart the 3-day CD clock: the APR becomes inaccurate beyond tolerance, the LOAN PRODUCT changes, or a PREPAYMENT PENALTY is added.

ECOA - bars discrimination in lending on race, colour, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or receipt of public assistance. A denied applicant is entitled to SPECIFIC reasons, or notice of the right to request them within 60 days.
Usury laws cap the maximum lawful interest rate.

national/financing.summary: Two documents do two jobs: the NOTE is the promise to repay, the SECURITY INSTRUMENT pledges the property. Everything else - clauses, loan types, disclosure rules - hangs off that split. Georgia uses a security deed rather than a mortgage.
traps: Points are a percentage of the LOAN, not the sale price. This is the single most common math error on the exam.
PMI protects the LENDER, never the borrower.
Assumption leaves the seller secondarily liable. Only NOVATION releases them.
Loan Estimate = 3 days after application. Closing Disclosure = 3 days before closing. Don't merge them.
vocab: The borrower's written promise to repay the debt.
Georgia's instrument conveying title to the lender as security.
A three-party security instrument using a trustee.
Makes the entire balance due on default.
Due-on-sale; makes the balance due on transfer.
Requires release of the lien when the debt is paid.
Buyer takes over the loan and becomes primarily liable.
Substituting a new party and releasing the original.
Taking title without personal liability on the loan.
A judgment for the shortfall after a foreclosure sale.
Level payments that retire the debt by maturity.
A large final payment on a partially amortized loan.
1% of the loan amount, paid to raise the lender's yield.
A lender's charge for making the loan, as a % of the loan.
Loan divided by the lesser of price or appraised value.
Private mortgage insurance on conventional loans above 80% LTV; protects the lender.
The VA's one-time charge in place of mortgage insurance.
An ARM's moving benchmark plus the lender's fixed markup.
Seller financing taken back at closing.
One loan covering several parcels, with a release clause.
A new loan encompassing an existing one that stays in place.
Where loans are originated to consumers.
Where existing loans are bought and sold, providing liquidity.
TILA's implementing rule; governs APR and credit advertising.
Governs settlement services and bans kickbacks for referrals.
TRID disclosure due within 3 business days of application.
TRID form the borrower must receive 3 business days before closing.
Equal Credit Opportunity Act; bars discrimination in lending.
Charging interest above the legal maximum.

national/landuse.blurb: Zoning, deed restrictions, eminent domain, police power, CC&Rs.

examples.k: The owner loses. A taking requires denial of ALL economically viable use, not a large loss of value.
examples.s: A city downzones an area. An owner's lot stays usable but is worth 40% less. The owner sues claiming a taking.
examples.t: Value loss is not a taking
w: Ask the only question that matters: does ANY economically viable use remain?
It does - the lot is still usable, just less profitably.
Diminution in value alone, even substantial, is a cost of regulation.

examples.k: Destruction, abandonment, and changing to a different nonconforming use are the three classic ways the protection is lost.
examples.s: A legal nonconforming gas station burns down. The owner wants to rebuild it exactly as it was.
w: Nonconforming rights exist to phase a use out, not preserve it forever.
Most ordinances end the status on destruction beyond a stated percentage.
Rebuilding therefore requires conforming to current zoning, or a variance.

ga: Georgia subdivisions are typically described by LOT AND BLOCK from a plat recorded with the clerk of superior court in the county where the land lies.
national/landuse.label: Land use controls

check.q: Which power requires the government to pay just compensation?
check.why: Only eminent domain takes and must pay. Police power regulates for free.

check.q: Property passing to the state when someone dies with no will and no heirs is:
check.why: Escheat prevents land from being ownerless.

l: Police power - regulate for health, safety, morals, and general welfare. Zoning, building codes, and environmental rules. NO compensation is paid.
Eminent domain - TAKE private property for public use. Just compensation IS required. The lawsuit that exercises it is CONDEMNATION.
Taxation - levy against property to fund government.
Escheat - property passes to the state when an owner dies with no will and no locatable heirs.

check.q: An owner needs relief from a setback requirement. They seek a:
check.why: A variance addresses a dimensional hardship.

check.q: A store that predates new residential zoning may continue as a:
check.why: A lawful pre-existing use is grandfathered.

l: Comprehensive (master) plan - the long-range policy document. Zoning is the ordinance that IMPLEMENTS the plan parcel by parcel.

Nonconforming use - a lawful use that predates the new zoning may continue ('grandfathered'). It is usually LOST on destruction beyond a set percentage, on abandonment for a stated period, or on change to a different nonconforming use.
Variance - permission to deviate from a DIMENSIONAL requirement (setback, height) because strict compliance creates a unique hardship the owner did not cause.
Special use / conditional use permit - allows a listed USE that needs review, such as a church or a school in a residential zone.
Spot zoning - rezoning one parcel inconsistently with the plan for one owner's benefit. Generally invalid.
Downzoning - reducing permitted intensity across an area.
Buffer zone - a strip separating incompatible districts.
Setback - the required distance from a lot line to a structure.

choices: Reduces value by more than a third
check.q: A regulation becomes a taking when it:
check.why: Loss of value alone, even large, is not a taking.

check.q: An owner suing on the ground that a regulation went too far brings an action in:
check.why: Inverse condemnation claims a regulatory taking.

p: A regulation is a valid exercise of police power even if it reduces value. It becomes a TAKING requiring compensation only when it denies ALL economically viable use. An owner claiming a regulation went that far sues in INVERSE CONDEMNATION.

choices: Any benefited lot owner or the HOA
check.q: Recorded subdivision covenants are enforced by:
check.why: CC&Rs are private; government does not enforce them.

check.q: Where a covenant and zoning conflict, which controls?
check.why: The more restrictive requirement governs.

l: CC&Rs / restrictive covenants - recorded private restrictions that RUN WITH THE LAND and bind later buyers. Any benefited owner (or the HOA) may enforce them, usually by injunction. Government does not enforce them.
Defences to enforcement: abandonment through widespread non-enforcement, and laches where delay has prejudiced the defendant.
Where a covenant and zoning conflict, the MORE RESTRICTIVE one controls.

check.q: The document confirming a building may lawfully be occupied is the:
check.why: The permit starts the work; the certificate of occupancy ends it.

choices: Major federal actions significantly affecting the environment
check.q: An Environmental Impact Statement is required for:
check.why: NEPA applies to major FEDERAL actions.

l: Building permit and inspections exist for public safety, not revenue. The CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY at the end confirms lawful occupancy.
NEPA requires an Environmental Impact Statement for major FEDERAL actions significantly affecting the environment.

national/landuse.summary: Two systems restrict what an owner may do: PUBLIC controls imposed by government, and PRIVATE controls created by contract or deed. The most common exam error is mixing them up - zoning is public and enforced by the municipality, CC&Rs are private and enforced by owners or an HOA.
traps: Eminent domain is the POWER; condemnation is the PROCEEDING.
A variance is for dimensional hardship; a special use permit is for a different type of use. Questions swap them constantly.
Zoning is public and enforced by government. CC&Rs are private and enforced by owners.
vocab: Government's power to regulate land use for public welfare without paying.
The power to take private property for public use with just compensation.
The legal proceeding that exercises eminent domain.
An owner's suit claiming regulation has effectively taken the property.
Transfer to the state when an owner dies with no will and no heirs.
The long-range policy guide that zoning implements.
A lawful pre-existing use that does not meet current zoning.
Permission to deviate from a dimensional zoning requirement on hardship grounds.
Approval for a listed conditional use in a district.
Rezoning one parcel inconsistently with the plan; generally invalid.
Reducing the permitted intensity of use across an area.
A transitional strip between incompatible zoning districts.
The required distance between a lot line and a structure.
Covenants, conditions and restrictions - recorded private land use controls.
A restriction or benefit that binds and passes to later owners.
The document confirming a structure may lawfully be occupied.
The NEPA study required for major federal actions.
A recorded subdivision map showing lots, blocks, and easements.

national/math.blurb: Commissions, prorations, LTV, points, area, appreciation.

examples.k: $7,869.40. The wrong answers are the totals from each earlier step - stopping early is the trap.
examples.s: $511,000 sale, 5.5% total commission. The listing brokerage keeps 40% and pays the rest to the co-op brokerage. The listing agent's split is 70% to the agent.
w: Listing brokerage = $28,105 x 40% = $11,242

examples.k: Adding 7% to $480,000 gives $513,600 - always offered, always wrong.
examples.s: The seller wants to net $478,000 after $2,000 of costs and a 7% commission.
w: The seller must clear $478,000 + $2,000 = $480,000
That $480,000 is the 93% left after commission

examples.k: $940.67 as a seller DEBIT and buyer CREDIT, because the buyer will pay the whole bill later.
examples.s: Annual taxes $4,980, unpaid. Closing March 9, 360-day year, seller responsible through the day before closing.
w: Seller's days = 2 full months x 30 + 8 = 68 days
Seller's share = $13.83 x 68 = $940.67

ga: Georgia transfer tax is $1.00 per $1,000 of consideration - divide the price by 1,000.
Georgia property taxes become a lien on JANUARY 1, which is why closings prorate them.
national/math.label: Real estate math

check.q: One acre equals:
check.why: A mile is 5,280 FEET; a section is 640 ACRES.

check.q: One section equals:
check.why: One square mile. A township is 36 sections.

l: 1 acre = 43,560 square feet
1 mile = 5,280 feet
1 section = 640 acres = 1 square mile
1 township = 36 sections
1 square yard = 9 square feet
Area of a rectangle = length x width. Triangle = 1/2 base x height.

check.q: Commission is a percentage of the:
check.why: Points are on the loan; commission is on the price.

check.q: $300,000 sale at 6%, split 50/50 between two brokerages. Each brokerage gets:
check.why: $18,000 total, halved.

p: Commission is always a percentage of the SALE price, then split - first between brokerages, then between each brokerage and its agent. Work outward one step at a time and do not stop at the total.

check.q: Discount points are a percentage of the:
check.why: The single most common math error on the exam.

check.q: Georgia transfer tax is a percentage of the:
check.why: $1.00 per $1,000 of consideration.

sections.h: Percentage of loan vs. percentage of price
l: Discount points and origination fees: percentage of the LOAN.
Commission and transfer tax: percentage of the SALE price.
LTV: loan divided by the LESSER of price and appraised value.

check.q: To find the price giving a target net after commission, you:
check.why: Adding always understates the price.

check.q: Seller wants $190,000 net with a 5% commission. Price is:
check.why: $190,000 / 0.95. Adding 5% gives $199,500 - the trap.

sections.h: Net to seller - divide, never add
p: To find the price that produces a target net, add the seller's costs to the target, then DIVIDE by (100% - commission%). Adding the commission percentage back on always understates the price, because the commission is a percentage of the larger sale price, not of the net.

check.q: Unpaid taxes at closing produce a:
check.why: The buyer will pay the whole bill later.

check.q: The seller owns the property through:
check.why: The buyer owns closing day forward.

l: Work out the daily rate, count the days, assign them to the right party.
A 360-day banker's year (30-day months) is the exam default unless told otherwise.
The SELLER owns through the day BEFORE closing; the buyer owns closing day forward.
UNPAID item (taxes in arrears): the seller owes for their time -> seller DEBIT, buyer CREDIT.
PREPAID item (rent collected, insurance paid ahead): the seller already has the benefit -> seller CREDIT... except rent, where the seller HOLDS the buyer's cash, so seller DEBIT, buyer CREDIT.
Ask 'who has the money, and who will get the benefit?' and the direction follows.

check.q: One month's interest equals:
check.why: Use the current balance.

check.q: $200,000 at 6% - one month's interest is:

p: Interest for one month = principal x annual rate / 12. In an amortized loan the interest portion shrinks as principal is repaid, so 'interest on the NEXT payment' uses the CURRENT balance.

check.q: Compound appreciation applies the rate to:
check.why: Multiply by (1 + rate) once per year.

choices: The same dollar amount off each year
check.q: Straight-line depreciation takes:
check.why: Basis divided by useful life.

l: COMPOUND appreciation applies the rate to the NEW value each year: multiply by (1 + rate) once per year.
STRAIGHT-LINE depreciation takes the same dollar amount off the original basis every year: basis / useful life.
Simple (non-compound) growth multiplies the original by (1 + rate x years) - the classic wrong answer on a compound question.

check.q: The front-end ratio compares housing expense to:
check.why: Convert annual to monthly first.

check.q: The back-end ratio adds:
check.why: Car loans, student loans, credit cards.

p: Front-end ratio = housing expense (PITI) / gross monthly income. Back-end adds all recurring monthly debt. Convert annual income to monthly FIRST.

national/math.summary: Real estate math is arithmetic with vocabulary attached. Almost every mistake is choosing the wrong BASE - a percentage of the loan versus the price, or of the net versus the sale price. Identify the base first, then compute.
traps: Points on the LOAN, commission on the PRICE. Mixing these is the top math error.
Net-to-seller is division, not addition.
Compound appreciation multiplies each year; simple growth does not.
Convert annual income to monthly before applying a qualifying ratio.
vocab: A measure of frontage along a street or water.
The original cost used to compute depreciation or gain.
Equal annual deductions over a useful life.
Dividing a shared expense between buyer and seller at closing.
An amount a party owes at closing.
An amount reducing what a party owes.
Housing expense divided by gross monthly income.
All recurring debt divided by gross monthly income.

national/ownership.blurb: Estates, tenancy, condos/co-ops, fixtures, water and air rights.

examples.k: Durational words (so long as, while, during, until) = determinable = automatic. Conditional words (but if, provided that, on condition that) = condition subsequent = the grantor must act.
examples.s: Ann conveys land 'to the city so long as it is used as a park.' The city later builds offices on it.
w: 'So long as' is durational language, so this is a fee simple DETERMINABLE.
A determinable fee ends AUTOMATICALLY the moment the condition is broken.
Title reverts to Ann (or her heirs) with no lawsuit required.

examples.k: The son receives nothing in this property. A will only passes what the person still owned at death.
examples.s: Two sisters own a lake house as joint tenants. One dies leaving a will giving 'all my real property' to her son.
w: Survivorship operates at the instant of death.
At that instant the deceased sister's interest disappears into the survivor's.
There is nothing left for the will to pass.

examples.k: The tenant may remove it before the lease ends and must repair the damage. If they leave it past lease end, it can become the landlord's.
examples.s: A commercial tenant bolts refrigeration units to the floor of a leased space. The lease is silent. The lease ends.
w: Bolting looks like annexation, which would normally make it a fixture.
But the tenant is COMMERCIAL and installed it to run the business.
That makes it a TRADE FIXTURE, which stays the tenant's personal property.

ga: Georgia does NOT recognise tenancy by the entirety. Married Georgians who want survivorship hold as joint tenants with right of survivorship, stated expressly in the deed.

A Georgia licensee who buys, sells, or leases property for their own account must disclose their licensed status in writing in the contract or lease, and must place any trust funds in an account approved by their broker.
national/ownership.label: Property ownership

check.q: Which right lets an owner keep other people off the land?
check.why: Exclude is the right to keep others out. Dispose is the right to sell or will it.

choices: The bundle's rights can be separated and sold individually
Mineral rights were never part of ownership
Only fee simple defeasible allows it
check.q: An owner sells the mineral rights but keeps the surface. This is possible because:
check.why: The sticks in the bundle can be split off and conveyed on their own.

l: Dispose - sell, gift, will, or encumber it
Use - occupy and use it for any lawful purpose
Possess - occupy it and exclude others
Exclude - keep others off
Sell/transfer - convey title to someone else
p: Ownership is not one right but several that can be separated and sold independently. Remember them as DUPES.

check.q: 'To the city so long as it is used as a park' creates a:
check.why: Durational words - so long as, while, until - create a determinable fee that ends automatically.

check.q: A life estate measured by someone else's life is:
check.why: Pur autre vie means 'for another's life'.

sections.h: Freehold estates: ownership without a fixed end
l: Fee simple absolute - the whole bundle, no conditions, no time limit. The most complete ownership the law recognises.

Fee simple defeasible - ownership that can be LOST if a condition happens. A DETERMINABLE fee ends automatically the instant the condition occurs (the grantor holds a possibility of reverter). A fee on CONDITION SUBSEQUENT does not end automatically - the grantor must act on a right of re-entry.

Life estate - lasts for someone's lifetime. Measured by the holder's life, or by a third party's life (pur autre vie). When it ends, the property goes to the REMAINDERMAN, or back to the grantor as a REVERSION.
p: A freehold lasts for an indefinite time. The three you must know:

check.q: A 60-day lease with fixed start and end dates is an:
check.why: Fixed start and end makes it an estate for years, regardless of length.

check.q: A tenant who stays after the lease ends without permission holds an:
check.why: Sufferance: possession with no right, but entry was originally lawful.

sections.h: Leasehold estates: possession with an end date
l: Estate for years - fixed start and end. Ends automatically; no notice needed. 'Years' is misleading: a 30-day lease with fixed dates is an estate for years.
Periodic estate - renews itself (month to month) until someone gives notice.
Estate at will - continues at the pleasure of both parties, endable any time.
Estate at sufferance - a holdover who stays without permission. Lowest estate: possession with no right, but entry was originally lawful so it is not trespass.
p: A leasehold gives possession, not ownership. The landlord keeps the LEASED FEE; the tenant holds the leasehold.

check.q: Which form has NO right of survivorship?
check.why: Tenancy in common shares pass by will or inheritance.

check.q: One joint tenant sells her share to a stranger. The buyer becomes a:
check.why: Selling severs the unities as to that share; the buyer takes as a tenant in common.

l: Tenancy in common - shares may be unequal, NO survivorship, each share passes by will or inheritance. The default when a deed says nothing.

Joint tenancy - equal shares with RIGHT OF SURVIVORSHIP. Requires the four unities: Possession, Interest, Time, Title (PITT). Selling a share severs the joint tenancy as to that share; the buyer becomes a tenant in common.
Tenancy by the entirety - joint tenancy between spouses that neither can sever alone. GEORGIA DOES NOT RECOGNISE IT.
Community property - a marital form used in nine states; Georgia is not one.
p: Ask two questions: is there a right of survivorship, and can one owner convey their share alone?

choices: Shares of stock plus a proprietary lease
An undivided share of the land
check.q: A cooperative resident owns:
check.why: A co-op owner holds personal property - stock - not real property.

check.q: A condo owner's percentage of the common elements mainly determines:
check.why: The percentage set in the declaration drives assessments and voting.

l: Condominium - you own your unit in fee simple, PLUS an undivided tenancy-in-common share of the common elements. That percentage, set in the declaration, drives your assessments and usually your voting weight, and cannot be sold separately from the unit.
Cooperative - a corporation owns the whole building. You own SHARES of stock plus a proprietary lease on your unit. You own personal property, not real property.
Timeshare estate - a deeded fractional real property interest. A right-to-use timeshare is only a contract right to occupy, which expires with the contract.

check.q: Which test carries the most weight in deciding whether something is a fixture?
check.why: MAI: method, adaptation, intent - and intent weighs heaviest.

choices: A trade fixture the tenant may remove
A fixture that stays with the building
check.q: A restaurant tenant's bolted-down pizza oven is:
check.why: Commercial tenants' business equipment stays their personal property.

l: Method of annexation - how firmly is it attached?
Adaptation - is it specially fitted to this property?
Intent - what did the person attaching it intend? Intent carries the most weight.

TRADE FIXTURES are the exception: items a COMMERCIAL TENANT installs to run their business stay the tenant's personal property and may be removed before the lease ends, with damage repaired. Left past lease end, they can be forfeited.
p: A fixture is personal property that has become part of the real estate, so it conveys with the property unless the contract excludes it. Courts weigh three things, remembered as MAI:

check.q: The parcel that BENEFITS from an easement appurtenant is the:
check.why: Dominant benefits; servient is burdened.

check.q: A utility company's right to run a line across land is an:
check.why: It benefits a company, not a parcel, so there is no dominant tenement.

sections.h: Encumbrances: other people's claims on your land
l: Easement appurtenant - runs with the land and benefits an adjoining parcel. The benefited parcel is the DOMINANT tenement; the burdened one is the SERVIENT tenement. It passes automatically to later owners.
Easement in gross - benefits a person or company, not a parcel. No dominant tenement. Commercial ones (utilities) are assignable and survive a sale.
Easement by necessity - implied when a parcel is landlocked by the seller's own severance of the land.
Easement by prescription - acquired by long, open, hostile use.
Licence - mere permission to use land. Personal and revocable at any time.
Encroachment - an unauthorised physical intrusion, usually found by SURVEY.
Lien - a money claim against the property.
Deed restriction / CC&R - a private restriction enforceable by benefited owners.

check.q: Rights along a flowing river are:
check.why: Riparian = flowing water. Littoral = still water.

check.q: Rights along a lake are:
check.why: Littoral attaches to static bodies: lakes, seas, ponds.

l: Riparian rights - attach to FLOWING water (rivers, streams).
Littoral rights - attach to STILL water (lakes, seas, ponds).
Prior appropriation - the western doctrine where use is granted by permit regardless of whether you touch the water.
Air rights can be sold separately - that is how air-rights development works.

national/ownership.summary: Ownership is a bundle of separate rights, and almost every question here asks which sticks in the bundle a party actually holds. Work out three things for any scenario: how long the interest lasts, whether anything can cut it short, and who else has a claim on the same land.
traps: 'Estate for years' does not mean years. A 60-day lease with fixed dates is one.
The landlord holds the LEASED FEE; the tenant holds the leasehold. Questions try to flip these.
A condominium owner owns real property; a co-op shareholder owns personal property (stock plus a lease).
Every encroachment is an encumbrance, but not every encumbrance is physical.
vocab: Ownership with no conditions and no time limit; the complete bundle of rights.
A fee that can be lost if a stated condition occurs.
The grantor's future interest after a determinable fee; takes effect automatically.
The grantor's future interest after a fee on condition subsequent; must be exercised.
An interest lasting for a person's lifetime.
A life estate measured by the life of someone other than the holder.
The person who takes the property when a life estate ends.
The interest returning to the grantor when a lesser estate ends.
A life tenant's failure to maintain, pay taxes, or preserve the property; the remainderman may sue now.
The landlord's ownership interest, subject to the lease.
The tenant's right of possession for a term.
Possession by a holdover tenant with no right to be there.
Co-ownership with no survivorship; shares pass to heirs.
Co-ownership with right of survivorship, requiring the four unities.
Possession, Interest, Time, Title - all required for joint tenancy.
Breaking a joint tenancy, usually by one owner conveying their share.
Marital joint tenancy neither spouse can sever alone. Not recognised in Georgia.
The parts of a condominium owned by all unit owners as tenants in common.
The occupancy right a cooperative shareholder holds.
Personal property that has become part of the realty and conveys with it.
A commercial tenant's business equipment; remains personal property and is removable.
Annual crops, treated as the tenant-farmer's personal property.
Any claim, lien, easement, or restriction limiting the fee.
The parcel benefited by an easement appurtenant.
The parcel burdened by an easement.
An easement benefiting a person or company rather than a parcel.
A physical intrusion onto a neighbouring parcel.
Revocable permission to use land; not an interest in land.

national/practice.blurb: Advertising, fair housing, antitrust, licensing, trust funds.

examples.k: Lawful company policy. What would make it illegal is evidence the firms coordinated with each other.
examples.s: A brokerage tells its agents never to quote below 5%. Competitors independently do the same.
w: Antitrust requires an AGREEMENT between competitors.
One firm setting its own rate is competition, not conspiracy.
Parallel behaviour alone is not proof of an agreement.

examples.k: The landlord must show a substantial, legitimate business need that no less discriminatory rule would serve.
examples.s: A manager requires income of three times the rent. It statistically screens out a protected class at a much higher rate.
w: The policy is facially neutral and applied to everyone.
But fair housing reaches EFFECTS, not just intent.
That is a disparate impact claim.

ga: Georgia permits net listings only under strict disclosure conditions.
Georgia advertising must identify the firm; a licensee may not appear to operate independently of their broker.
A Georgia salesperson may be paid ONLY by their affiliated broker.
national/practice.label: Practice of real estate

check.q: Which is NOT one of the seven federal protected classes?
check.why: Some states and cities protect it, but not federal housing law.

check.q: Familial status protects:
check.why: Also pregnant people and those securing custody.

l: The SEVEN protected classes: race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, and handicap.
Familial status covers households with children under 18, pregnant people, and those securing custody. Exception: qualified housing for older persons (55+/62+).

Handicap includes HIV/AIDS. Landlords must allow reasonable MODIFICATIONS at the TENANT'S expense, and make reasonable ACCOMMODATIONS to rules at the LANDLORD'S expense (waiving a no-pets rule for an assistance animal - and no pet fee).
Source of income and marital status are NOT federally protected in housing, though some states and cities protect them.
The 1866 Civil Rights Act bars ALL racial discrimination with no exceptions.

check.q: Telling owners a protected group is moving in to induce sales is:
check.why: Illegal whether or not the claim is true.

check.q: A neutral policy that falls hardest on a protected class may be:
check.why: Intent is not required for a violation.

l: STEERING - channelling people toward or away from areas by protected class. It does not require saying anything negative; selectively providing information does it.
BLOCKBUSTING (panic peddling) - inducing sales by suggesting a protected group's entry will harm the neighbourhood. Illegal whether or not the claim is true.
REDLINING - a lender refusing or pricing loans by area demographics.
Discriminatory advertising - describe the PROPERTY, never the desired occupant.

DISPARATE IMPACT - a neutral policy that falls disproportionately on a protected class can violate the Act with NO intent to discriminate. The defence is a substantial, legitimate business need with no less discriminatory alternative.

check.q: Federal fair housing complaints go to:
check.why: The commission can also discipline the licence separately.

check.q: A HUD complaint is generally filed within:
check.why: One year of the discriminatory act.

p: HUD handles federal complaints, generally filed within one year. A licensee's conduct can also independently cost them their licence through the state commission, and private suits are available.

choices: Price fixing, a per se violation
check.q: Two competing brokerages agreeing on a commission rate is:
check.why: No defence and no disclosure cure.

check.q: A single firm setting its own minimum rate is:
check.why: Antitrust requires an agreement between competitors.

l: PRICE FIXING - competitors agreeing on commission rates. A per se violation: no defence, no disclosure cure. Commission is always negotiated between a broker and a client.
GROUP BOYCOTT - competitors conspiring to refuse to deal with someone.
MARKET ALLOCATION - dividing territories or customer types.
TIE-IN - conditioning one sale on the purchase of another product.
A SINGLE FIRM setting its own rate is lawful company policy, not conspiracy. Antitrust requires an AGREEMENT between competitors; parallel behaviour alone is not proof.

check.q: Under which listing is the broker paid no matter who sells?
check.why: Exclusive agency lets the seller sell it themselves commission-free.

choices: Keeps everything above the seller's stated price
check.q: A net listing is one where the broker:
check.why: Heavily restricted; Georgia allows it only under strict disclosure.

l: OPEN - many brokers; the seller owes nothing if the seller finds the buyer.
EXCLUSIVE AGENCY - one broker, but the seller may still sell it themselves commission-free.
EXCLUSIVE RIGHT TO SELL - one broker paid no matter who sells. Most common.
NET LISTING - the broker keeps everything above a price the seller sets. Illegal in many states; Georgia permits it only under strict disclosure.
Buyer agency agreements mirror these structures.

choices: Hold the funds and use interpleader
check.q: When buyer and seller both demand a disputed deposit, the broker should:
check.why: Picking a side invites a conversion claim.

choices: A separate trust or escrow account
check.q: Client funds belong in:
check.why: Mixing is commingling.

p: Client money goes into a separate trust or escrow account, never the operating account. COMMINGLING is mixing; CONVERSION is spending. When buyer and seller both demand a disputed deposit, the broker must NOT pick a side - hold the funds and use interpleader or the state's prescribed procedure.

choices: Discuss price or terms with a buyer
check.q: An unlicensed assistant may NOT:
check.why: Anything involving negotiation or advice requires a licence.

choices: There is an established business relationship or written consent
check.q: Under the do-not-call rules a licensee may call a registered number if:
check.why: FSBO and expired-listing calls are a common violation source.

l: Advertising must identify the firm and must never mislead or imply a licensee operates independently of their broker. Claiming credit for another firm's sale is a misrepresentation.
Do-not-call rules: an established business relationship or express written consent is needed. FSBO and expired-listing calls are a common violation source.

Unlicensed assistants may do clerical and ministerial work - scheduling, preparing materials for approval, basic factual answers. They may NOT negotiate, solicit, discuss terms, or host an open house unaccompanied.

Independent contractor status: the broker controls RESULTS, not hours and methods, but must still supervise for licence-law compliance. The IRS safe harbour needs a licence, pay based on output, and a written IC agreement.
ADA Title III requires removing barriers in public accommodations where READILY ACHIEVABLE; new construction faces stricter standards.

national/practice.summary: This block covers how you are allowed to run the business: fair housing, antitrust, advertising, trust funds, listings, and supervision. The recurring theme is that good intentions are no defence - conduct is judged by its effect.
traps: Source of income and marital status are not among the seven federal classes.
Occupancy limits by NUMBER of people can be lawful; limits by AGE of occupant are not.
Modification = physical = tenant pays. Accommodation = rules = landlord absorbs.
Intent is not required for a fair housing violation.
vocab: A group the law shields from housing discrimination.
Households with children under 18, pregnant people, those seeking custody.
A physical change for a disabled tenant, at the tenant's expense.
A change to rules or policies, at the provider's expense.
Channelling buyers toward or away from areas by protected class.
Inducing panic selling by claims about a protected group moving in.
Refusing or pricing loans by neighbourhood demographics.
A neutral policy with a discriminatory effect; intent not required.
Competitors agreeing on prices; a per se antitrust violation.
Competitors agreeing to refuse to deal with someone.
Conditioning one transaction on another purchase.
Non-exclusive; seller owes nothing if they sell it themselves.
One broker, but the seller may sell it themselves commission-free.
One broker is paid regardless of who sells.
Broker keeps everything above the seller's stated net; heavily restricted.
Mixing trust funds with the broker's own money.
A court action letting a stakeholder deposit disputed funds for decision.
Clerical, non-discretionary tasks an unlicensed assistant may do.
A licensee whose results, not methods, the broker directs.
The ADA standard for barrier removal: easily accomplishable.

national/transfer.blurb: Deeds, title insurance, recording, closing, adverse possession.

examples.k: If the Monday buyer had no notice (including no reason to see the possession), they win. If the possession was open and obvious, they lose. Notice decides it.
examples.s: A buyer records Monday. An earlier buyer of the same parcel, who had paid and moved in, records Wednesday. Race-notice state.
w: Race-notice protects a later buyer only if they took WITHOUT NOTICE and recorded first.
The Monday buyer did record first.
But the earlier buyer's open POSSESSION is constructive notice.

examples.k: The seller must obtain and RECORD a release or satisfaction. A buyer cannot be forced to take title subject to an undischarged mortgage.
examples.s: A title commitment lists an unreleased 1978 mortgage as a Schedule B exception.
examples.t: Insurance does not clear a lien
w: An EXCEPTION is exactly what the policy will NOT cover.
So buying insurance does not solve the problem.
Marketable title requires clearing the lien of record.

ga: Georgia records with the CLERK OF SUPERIOR COURT in the county where the land lies.
Georgia adverse possession: 20 years, or 7 years under colour of title.
Georgia real estate transfer tax is $1.00 per $1,000 of consideration, customarily paid by the SELLER and collected when the deed is recorded.
Georgia closings are supervised by a licensed ATTORNEY, who customarily represents the LENDER, not the buyer.
national/transfer.label: Transfer of title

check.q: Title actually passes on:
check.why: Recording gives notice; it does not pass title.

check.q: Who signs the deed?
check.why: The grantee never signs.

l: In writing, with a competent GRANTOR
A named, identifiable GRANTEE
Words of conveyance (the granting clause)
An adequate legal description
The grantor's SIGNATURE
DELIVERY to and ACCEPTANCE by the grantee - this is what actually passes title
Notarisation (acknowledgment) is needed to RECORD, not for validity. The grantee does not sign. Consideration need only be recited.

check.q: Which deed offers the grantee the most protection?
check.why: It warrants against defects through the entire chain.

check.q: A quitclaim deed is most often used to:
check.why: It releases whatever interest the grantor may have.

sections.h: Types of deed, strongest to weakest
l: GENERAL WARRANTY - warrants title against all defects through the ENTIRE chain, including before the grantor owned it. Strongest.
SPECIAL (limited) WARRANTY - warrants only against defects arising during the GRANTOR'S ownership.
BARGAIN AND SALE - implies the grantor holds title but gives no warranty.
QUITCLAIM - conveys whatever interest the grantor has, if any, with NO warranty. The tool for clearing clouds.
Special-purpose deeds: executor's, sheriff's, tax, gift, and trustee's deeds.

check.q: The covenant of seisin is breached, if at all:
check.why: It is a PRESENT covenant, so the clock starts at delivery.

check.q: Quiet enjoyment is a:
check.why: Future covenants are breached only on later disturbance.

l: PRESENT covenants - breached at delivery if at all, so the clock starts then: seisin (the grantor owns and can convey), right to convey, and against encumbrances.

FUTURE covenants - breached only on a later disturbance: quiet enjoyment (undisturbed possession and defence against lawful claims), warranty forever, and further assurance (the grantor will sign whatever is later needed).

check.q: Recording gives:
check.why: Everyone is charged with knowledge whether they looked or not.

choices: Took without notice AND recorded first
check.q: Under a race-notice statute a later buyer wins only if they:
check.why: Both conditions are required.

l: Recording gives CONSTRUCTIVE notice - everyone is charged with knowledge whether or not they looked.
ACTUAL notice is what a person genuinely knows. Open POSSESSION by someone can itself be constructive notice, which defeats a later buyer who ignored it.
Race - first to record wins.
Notice - a later buyer without notice wins.
RACE-NOTICE - a later buyer wins only if they took WITHOUT NOTICE and recorded FIRST.
Generally, first in time, first in right - subject to those statutes. Property tax liens usually take priority over everything.

choices: Something the policy will NOT cover
check.q: A Schedule B exception in a title commitment is:
check.why: The word means the opposite of what it sounds like.

choices: Defects that already existed when issued
check.q: Title insurance protects against:
check.why: It is retrospective, paid once.

l: Chain of title - the sequence of owners.
Abstract of title - the condensed written history of every recorded document.
Opinion of title - an attorney's interpretation of the abstract.
Title commitment - the insurer's promise to issue a policy, with Schedule B EXCEPTIONS listing what it will NOT cover.

Title insurance - protects against defects that ALREADY EXISTED when issued: forgery, undisclosed heirs, recording errors. Paid once. An OWNER'S policy covers the buyer; a LENDER'S policy covers only the lender.
Marketable title - title a reasonable buyer would accept. An unreleased mortgage of record must be cleared with a recorded release; insurance does not fix it.
Cloud on title - removed by a QUITCLAIM from the claimant, or a QUIET TITLE suit. A LIS PENDENS creates a cloud by giving notice of pending litigation.

check.q: Georgia's adverse possession period under colour of title is:
check.why: 20 years without colour of title.

check.q: Sudden loss or addition of land that does NOT move boundaries is:
check.why: Gradual change moves boundaries; sudden change does not.

l: Adverse possession - open, notorious, hostile, actual, and continuous possession for the statutory period, plus any state-specific element. EVERY element is required. GEORGIA: 20 years, or 7 years under COLOUR OF TITLE.

Accretion - gradual gain of land by deposit (the new soil is alluvion). Erosion is gradual loss. AVULSION is sudden change and does NOT move boundaries. Reliction is land exposed by permanently receding water.
Death: TESTATE (with a will) - real property passes by DEVISE. INTESTATE - state succession law controls. Escheat if no will and no heirs.
Foreclosure, tax sale, eminent domain, and dedication.

check.q: Which system is most common in Georgia subdivisions?
check.why: Georgia does not use the rectangular survey system.

choices: Return to the point of beginning
check.q: A metes and bounds description must:
check.why: It must close.

l: METES AND BOUNDS - distances and directions from a POINT OF BEGINNING; must return to it to close.
LOT AND BLOCK - references a recorded plat. The most common system in Georgia subdivisions.
RECTANGULAR (government) SURVEY - townships, ranges, and sections. A section is 1 square mile = 640 acres; a township is 36 sections. Georgia does NOT use it.

national/transfer.summary: Title passes on DELIVERY AND ACCEPTANCE of a valid deed. Recording is not required to make the deed good between the parties - it exists to give notice to everyone else and to settle priority when two people claim the same land.
traps: Recording is not required for a deed to be valid between grantor and grantee.
The grantee never signs the deed.
A title EXCEPTION is uncovered, not covered. The word means the opposite of what it sounds.
Avulsion is sudden and does not move boundaries; accretion is gradual and does.
vocab: The one conveying / the one receiving.
The words of conveyance in a deed.
Notarisation; required to record, not for validity.
Warrants title against all defects through the whole chain.
Warrants only against defects during the grantor's ownership.
Conveys whatever interest the grantor has, with no warranty.
The grantor's promise that they own and can convey.
Promise of undisturbed possession and defence of title.
Legal notice given by recording; everyone is charged with it.
A later buyer prevails only if without notice AND recording first.
A condensed history of all recorded documents.
The insurer's promise to issue a policy, listing exceptions.
A defect the title policy will not cover.
Title free enough of defects that a reasonable buyer would accept it.
A claim or defect casting doubt on ownership.
A suit asking a court to settle ownership.
Recorded notice of pending litigation; creates a cloud.
Acquiring title by long, open, hostile possession.
A written instrument that appears to convey title but is defective.
Gradual addition of land by water / the deposited soil.
Sudden loss or addition of land; boundaries do not change.
Dying with a will / without one.
A gift of real property by will.
Description by distances and directions from a point of beginning.
Description by reference to a recorded plat.

national/valuation.blurb: The three approaches to value, CMA, appraisal principles.

examples.k: $416,000. CIA: Comp Inferior, Add. Superior features come off.
examples.s: A comparable sold for $420,000. It has an extra half-bath worth $12,000, and its lot is inferior to the subject's by $8,000.
examples.t: Adjusting comparables in the right direction
w: Adjust the COMP toward the subject, never the subject toward the comp.
Comp is SUPERIOR on the bath: subtract $12,000 -> $408,000.
Comp is INFERIOR on the lot: add $8,000 -> $416,000.

examples.k: About $560,000. Skipping vacancy or expenses inflates the answer - which is exactly what the wrong choices will look like.
examples.s: A four-unit building rents for $1,400 per unit per month, vacancy is 5%, and operating expenses are $19,000 a year. Cap rate 8%.
examples.t: Cap rate value with a proper NOI
w: Potential gross = 4 x $1,400 x 12 = $67,200
Less 5% vacancy ($3,360) = $63,840 effective gross
Less $19,000 expenses = $44,840 NOI

examples.k: External obsolescence, incurable, deducted from the land - not the improvements.
examples.s: A house on a busy corner sells for less than identical houses mid-block.
w: The cause is outside the property line, so it is EXTERNAL obsolescence.
External obsolescence is always incurable - the owner cannot move the road.
Because a location penalty attaches to the site, it is charged against the LAND.

ga: A Georgia licensee preparing a CMA is giving a broker's pricing opinion. Presenting it as an appraisal, or implying appraiser credentials, is a licence-law problem.
national/valuation.label: Valuation & market analysis

check.q: What a property actually sold for is its:
check.why: Price is the historical fact; value is an opinion.

check.q: Insurable value covers:
check.why: Land does not burn, so it is excluded.

sections.h: Value, price, and cost are three different things
l: Market value - the most probable price in an arm's-length sale, with an informed buyer and seller, adequate exposure, and no duress. An OPINION.
Market price - what a property actually sold for. A historical FACT, which may reflect a distress sale.
Cost - what it took to build. Cost does not equal value.
Assessed value - the tax base, often a percentage of market value.
Insurable value - the improvements only, since land does not burn.

check.q: DUST stands for demand, utility, scarcity and:
check.why: Transferability - title must be conveyable.

check.q: A property nobody can legally convey lacks:
check.why: Without transferability there is no market value.

l: Demand - buyers who want it and can pay
Utility - it can satisfy a need
Scarcity - supply is limited
Transferability - title can be conveyed

check.q: A modest house among mansions gains value. This is:
check.why: Progression pulls the lesser property up.

check.q: Combining two lots so the whole exceeds the parts creates:
check.why: Assemblage is the act; plottage is the added value.

l: Substitution - value is capped by the cost of an equally desirable substitute. This underlies the whole sales comparison approach.
Highest and best use - the use that is legally permitted, physically possible, financially feasible, and maximally productive. Legality comes first; an illegal use is never highest and best.
Conformity - maximum value where properties are reasonably similar.
Progression - a modest property is pulled UP by superior neighbours.
Regression - a superior property is dragged DOWN by lesser neighbours.
Contribution - a component is worth what it ADDS to the whole, not what it cost.
Anticipation - value reflects expected future benefits.
Assemblage - combining parcels. PLOTTAGE is the extra value that results.
Supply and demand, and change - values move with the market and never sit still.

check.q: Valuing a 40-year-old church relies most on the:
check.why: Special-purpose property rarely sells and earns no rent.

check.q: A comparable is INFERIOR to the subject. You:
check.why: CIA - Comp Inferior, Add. Never adjust the subject.

l: SALES COMPARISON - compare recent similar sales. Best for houses and land. Always adjust the COMPARABLE, never the subject. Comp superior: SUBTRACT. Comp inferior: ADD. Memory hook CIA - Comp Inferior, Add.

COST - reproduction or replacement cost, LESS depreciation, PLUS land value. Best for new construction and special-purpose property (churches, schools, libraries) that rarely sells and produces no rent.
INCOME - convert income into value. Best for rentals and commercial. Use IRV: Income = Rate x Value, so Value = NOI / Rate.

check.q: Which is NEVER an operating expense?
check.why: Debt service comes out after NOI, not before.

check.q: Effective gross income is potential gross income less:
check.why: Vacancy first, then expenses give NOI.

l: Potential gross income (all units, fully rented)
minus vacancy and collection loss = EFFECTIVE GROSS INCOME
minus operating expenses = NET OPERATING INCOME
minus debt service = CASH FLOW
DEBT SERVICE IS NEVER AN OPERATING EXPENSE. Neither is depreciation or capital improvement. This is the single most common trap.
p: Nearly every income-approach mistake is a bad NOI. Work down the statement in order:

check.q: A new highway beside the house causes:
check.why: The cause is outside the property line, so it is external and incurable.

choices: Whether the cost is recovered in added value
Whether it can physically be fixed
check.q: Curable vs. incurable is decided by:
check.why: It is an economic test, not a physical one.

l: Physical deterioration - wear, tear, and deferred maintenance. Often curable.
Functional obsolescence - a defect in the design or utility of the structure itself: one bathroom, a bedroom you walk through, an outdated layout.

External (economic) obsolescence - caused by something OUTSIDE the property line: a new highway, a failing neighbourhood. ALWAYS INCURABLE, because the owner cannot fix it. It is charged against the LAND.
Curable vs. incurable is an ECONOMIC test, not a physical one: an item is curable when the cost to fix it is recovered in added value.

choices: A pricing opinion, not an appraisal
check.q: A broker's CMA is:
check.why: It must never be presented as an appraisal.

check.q: Who may perform an appraisal?
check.why: Appraisals require appraiser credentials.

p: A competitive market analysis is a broker's pricing opinion built from comparables to help set a list price. It is NOT an appraisal, must never be presented as one, and needs no appraiser licence. An appraisal is an independent opinion by a licensed or certified appraiser.

check.q: In reconciliation the appraiser:
check.why: Averaging is always wrong.

check.q: Reconciliation produces:
check.why: One conclusion, weighted by reliability.

sections.h: The appraisal process ends in reconciliation
p: Reconciliation weighs each approach by how RELIABLE it is for that property, and states a single value conclusion. Averaging the three is always wrong.

national/valuation.summary: Value is an OPINION of the most probable price, not a fact. Three approaches exist, and the whole skill is picking the right one for the property type and then weighting them honestly. Appraisers never average the three.
traps: Debt service is NEVER an operating expense when building NOI.
Cap rate and value move INVERSELY: a higher cap rate means a lower value.
Curability is about economics, not physics. If the fix costs more than it returns, it is incurable even though it is physically repairable.
Cost approach for a church or school; sales comparison for a house; income for a rental.
vocab: The most probable price under normal, arm's-length conditions.
The actual price a property sold for.
The value used as the property tax base.
The value of the improvements only.
Demand, Utility, Scarcity, Transferability - the four elements of value.
Value is limited by the cost of an equally desirable alternative.
Legally permitted, physically possible, financially feasible, maximally productive.
Value is maximised where properties are similar.
A lesser property gains value from superior neighbours.
A superior property loses value among lesser neighbours.
A component is worth what it adds to the whole.
Value based on expected future benefits.
Combining adjacent parcels under one owner.
The added value created by assemblage.
A recently sold similar property used in the sales comparison approach.
Cost to build an exact replica.
Cost to build equivalent utility with current materials.
Income if fully rented with no losses.
Potential gross income less vacancy and collection loss.
Effective gross income less operating expenses, before debt service.
The rate converting income to value; Value = NOI / Rate.
Sale price divided by gross rent; a quick screening tool.
Loss in value from wear and tear.
Loss in value from a defect in the structure's own design or utility.
Loss in value caused from outside the property; always incurable.
Weighting the approaches into one value conclusion.
A broker's comparative pricing opinion; not an appraisal.
